papers.title: Gaussian Is All You Need: Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation
papers.abstract: Preparing an entangled state faithfully requires an amount of resource given by its entanglement cost. With less entanglement, the best achievable fidelity is governed by the Rényi entanglement of formation of orders above one. We prove that, for any finite-energy multimode bosonic Gaussian state, all these quantities are additive and attained by a Gaussian pure-state decomposition. It follows that the closest separable state in fidelity to any Gaussian state is Gaussian, and that the strong converse exponent of entanglement dilution, which sets how fast the optimal fidelity decays below the cost, is exactly computable. For channels, we prove that pure Gaussian inputs minimize the output Rényi entropies of every multimode Gaussian channel at all orders $α\ge1$, and we obtain the optimal fidelity of simulating pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels with finite entanglement, for any number of uses.

papers.title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
papers.abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work reports encouraging advances, it remains unclear whether these stem from genuine noncommutative quantum geometry or from conventional classical regularization and scale effects. We test this in a controlled audit of matrix-form Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML) and variational quantum circuits on the Moscow Exchange (2020-2025), combining daily equity data with causally lagged macro news under realistic trading costs, short-selling bans, and abrupt shifts in market regimes. By using capacity-matched operator swaps -- which progressively eliminate complex Berry phases and matrix noncommutativity down to a commuting classical Gibbs radial-basis limit under scale-invariant regularization -- as well as testing spectral indicators against radial-norm null hypotheses and untrained GUE random matrices, we isolate the contribution of each quantum element. In out-of-sample data, neither complex phases, noncommutativity, nor circuit entanglement improves the ranking of returns relative to classical controls. Once feature magnitudes are normalized, apparent crisis detection from raw spectral gaps drops below chance levels. These results show that on noisy equity panels, matrix-form QCML acts as an adaptive spectrally bounded classical smoothing kernel: it reliably integrates lagged news and curbs extreme crisis forecasts without passing economic multiple-testing thresholds, while our audit provides operator-swap and random-matrix controls for evaluating future quantum-inspired financial models.

papers.title: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits. In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center. The model includes the NV electron spin, a coupled 13C nuclear spin, the hyperfine interaction, an effective microwave/radio-frequency-assisted SWAP interaction for writing and reading, a single effective phonon mode with longitudinal spin-phonon coupling, and Lindblad relaxation and dephasing channels. The dynamics are simulated with the Lindblad master equation in QuTiP, using the secular approximation and a hyperfine-resonant drive in the rotating frame. Without spin-phonon coupling and electron decoherence, the write-store-read protocol recovers the stored state with a fidelity above 0.9999. With the default decoherence rates, increasing the spin-phonon coupling from 0 to 0.06 MHz lowers the worst-case retrieval fidelity from 0.9994 to 0.9884, and the fidelity oscillates with the phonon-mode period because electron-phonon entanglement generated during the write step is partially undone during the read step. With a phenomenological temperature-dependent rate model, the fidelity decreases monotonically from 0.9997 at 1 K to 0.9938 at 300 K, while storage-time losses follow the assumed nuclear-spin decoherence rates. The storage-time plots, temperature sweep, and parameter maps identify operating regimes for NV-center quantum memory, and the accompanying open-source code provides a reproducible framework for studying phonon-limited quantum memory.

papers.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
papers.abstract: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs using beam-like Type-II SPDC in a $β$-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it exhibits a $\sim$1.56-fold enhancement in the detected single-photon count rate and a $\sim$1.45-fold enhancement in the coincidence count rate. Measurements of position correlations and momentum anti-correlations certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. These correlations are further exploited to demonstrate quantum imaging in both the position and momentum domains. These characteristics make the source a practical resource for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

papers.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below $10^{-10}$ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm $\times$ 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.

papers.title: Robust Certification of Non-projective Qubit Measurements without Inputs
papers.abstract: Positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) beyond projective simulation (aka non-projective measurements) offer advantages over projective measurements, motivating their certification directly from observed statistics. Here, we show that this certification can be achieved robustly without input randomness, using only the joint outcome distribution of two measurement devices. We consider two spatially separated observers whose only shared resource is an uncharacterised two-qubit state. Each observer performs a local measurement. In the projective-simulable case, the measurement device privately randomises over qubit projective measurements and applies arbitrary classical post-processing to their outcomes. In the noiseless regime, we identify three- and four-outcome anti-correlations that certify that both local measurements lie beyond projective simulation. To establish noise robustness, we develop a non-linear covariance witness that combines the geometry of projective measurements with a contraction bound valid for every two-qubit state. For the correlations generated by identical qubit trine measurements or identical qubit SIC-POVM on noisy qubit singlet, we obtain exact critical white-noise fractions of (1/4) and (1/3), respectively. Below these thresholds, no pair of projective-simulable measurements on any two-qubit state can reproduce these correlations. We present explicit projective simulations that attain the thresholds and cover the remaining noise range. Finally, the same method yields a strictly positive noise tolerance for certification whenever both observers apply the same extremal qubit POVM with three or four non-zero effects to a depolarised qubit singlet. These results establish a general analytic framework for certifying non-projective qubit measurement resources without input randomness.

papers.title: Laser-induced streaking of megaelectronvolt electrons in a liquid medium
papers.abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02044-5Researchers demonstrate the laser-induced streaking of megaelectronvolt electrons in liquids. The effect originates from a dielectric-mediated electron–light interaction rather than plasma lensing. Experimental conditions under which the streaking can be suppressed are identified.

papers.title: Using a static spacetime subsystem code to calculate Floquet code distance
papers.abstract: Dynamical codes, including Floquet codes, can capture time-dependent phenomena in quantum error correction circuits that are absent from static stabilizer or subsystem codes, such as detecting regions and error propagation. They are also capable of preserving more logical qubits than corresponding schemes in which the same syndrome-extraction measurements are performed without being distributed over time. However, evaluating the performance of dynamical codes is more complicated than for static codes because error detection depends on when an error occurs within the measurement schedule. In this work, we introduce a mapping from the measurement sequence of a Floquet code to a static spacetime subsystem code and show that calculating the distance of a Floquet code can be reduced to calculating the distance of the corresponding static subsystem code. Crucially, our mapping preserves code distance, a property that is not guaranteed for general spacetime code mappings. This reduction converts the dynamical distance problem into a static subsystem code problem, substantially simplifying the analysis of Floquet measurement schedules and facilitating the evaluation of fault tolerance for new measurement schemes.

papers.title: Quditology: harnessing many levels for quantum information processing
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers the prospect of surpassing classical computation on certain tasks by leveraging quantum coherence and entanglement. However, a significant gap remains between current quantum hardware and the requirements to transcend what classical computers can achieve, with decoherence limiting the capacity of storing quantum information and the number of logical steps that can be executed reliably. In the long term, fault tolerance bridges this gap, but simply changing the numerical base from binary to higher base d is a viable way to 'squeeze more juice'---get more quantum information processing---from a quantum computer of given size. Additionally, for quantum simulations, qudits offer a natural encoding scheme for high-dimensional physical degrees of freedom. Here, we review recent experimental progress in high-fidelity preparation, control, and measurement of qudits across various platforms such as trapped ions, superconducting circuits, solid-state nuclear spins, photonic systems, and neutral atoms. We highlight early demonstrations of qudit-based quantum simulation, computation and error suppression enabled by these developments, heralding the transition of qudits from conceptual constructs to viable building blocks for quantum technologies. Finally, we outline key challenges and potential future directions for scalable qudit quantum information processing.

papers.title: Class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables
papers.abstract: Photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables can carry two key bits per pair in entanglement-based quantum key distribution. We develop class-resolved sifting for such sources: every detected pair is assigned to a class according to which degrees of freedom were measured in compatible bases, and error and key rates are estimated separately in each class. Applied to previously reported data from a two-crystal spontaneous parametric down-conversion source read out in intermediate fractional-Fourier planes, the method recovers the key yield of independent sifting and turns the comparison between classes into a quantitative consistency test for cross-dependencies between the two degrees of freedom. The measured dependence lies below the spatial-polarization coupling predicted for the source, at the edge of the present statistical sensitivity. Resolving the data by polarization-analyzer setting, we find an approximately twofold dependence of the spatial error on the polarization setting in one readout arm, attributable to the measurement apparatus rather than to the source and relevant to basis-dependent side channels. We compare the hyperentangled protocol with a single 4-dimensional system measured in two mutually unbiased bases. Fundamentally, both yield the same key per detected pair and obey the same entropic bound, but they differ in their tensor-product structure: hyperentanglement factors the bases into separate two-outcome measurements, which are simpler to implement and allow errors to be attributed to each degree of freedom, whereas a single variable gives access to non-product bases that can increase the noise tolerance. For the present source, whose polarization coherence is limited by partial which-crystal erasure, a single-variable spatial encoding would yield more key only if its four-outcome readout kept the symbol error within a few percent.

papers.title: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries
papers.abstract: Simulating the dynamics of interacting fermions remains a central computational challenge across physics and chemistry. We introduce Dirac propagation, a classical method that simulates local observables in fermionic systems subject to particle-number-conserving unitaries. We show that, in the operator expansion, strings with weights above the total particle number can be discarded without incurring any error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff bounds the number of retained strings polynomially in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The formalism combines a compact representation with explicit expressions for interacting gates and exact treatment of number-conserving fermionic Gaussian and Clifford unitaries. This framework offers an approach to simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits.

papers.title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
papers.abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

papers.title: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive. Fault-tolerant algorithms for these tasks, including real-time dynamics and phase estimation, assume efficient preparation of the initial many-body state, making state preparation an important bottleneck. Matrix product states obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group can be compiled sequentially into fault-tolerant circuits. We exploit non-Abelian spin SU(2) symmetry in this compilation. By the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors, which carry the variational information, need generic unitary synthesis. The magnetic structure is restored by Clebsch-Gordan transformations with analytically known angles. We benchmark the method on representative strongly correlated models, including the one-dimensional Hubbard model, quasi-one-dimensional Hubbard geometries, and Anderson impurity models, and perform fault-tolerant resource estimates using the Toffoli count as the primary cost metric. Across the systems considered, exploiting non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry reduces the Toffoli cost roughly threefold relative to U(1)-adapted compilation and by more than an order of magnitude relative to the standard dense compilation method. These results demonstrate how non-Abelian symmetries can substantially reduce the cost of transferring classically tractable many-body ground states to quantum computers, facilitating their use in quantum dynamics and energy estimation.

papers.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
papers.abstract: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.

papers.title: Admissibility of Linear Time Series Models under Cone Constraints
papers.abstract: Time series analysis extends beyond vector-valued observations to evolving probability densities, quantile functions, and covariance operators. These objects carry intrinsic constraints, raising questions about the admissibility of additive linear models, which have long served as a foundation for time series modelling and theory. We give a necessary and sufficient support condition for a stationary Hilbert-space linear process to remain in a closed convex cone almost surely. Innovations with unbounded lower tails, including Gaussian innovations, confine randomness to the cone's largest linear subspace. For fractional filters with convergent normalized cumulative coefficients, the leading stochastic directions obey the same restriction, even with bounded innovations. For real-line quantiles, variation under unbounded lower tails and leading fractional accumulation can occur only through location shifts. For cone-valued processes, partial sums of centred stationary increments remain bounded in mean square when evaluated by any linear functional that is nonnegative on the cone, in contrast to the growing variance of a random walk. We derive an exact slope criterion for locally absolutely continuous quantiles and construct nondegenerate additive models with bounded innovations for quantiles, densities, and covariance matrices. These findings clarify the scope of ordinary additive modelling under structural constraints.

papers.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
papers.abstract: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance? We determine the optimal second-order coding rates for input dimension $d\ge2$, erasure probability $0<p<1/2$, and fixed infidelity (one minus fidelity) $0<\varepsilon<1$. For $n$ channel uses, the optimal base-two logarithmic code size is \begin{equation}\tag{A}\label{eq:abstract-rate} n(1-2p)\log_2d +2\sqrt{np(1-p)}\log_2d\,Φ^{-1}(\varepsilon) +O((\ln n)^2), \end{equation} where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $Φ^{-1}$ is its quantile function. The square-root term is the second-order correction. This formula holds for entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication. Quantum error measures failure to preserve entanglement. Private error compares the actual output with a correctly decoded uniform message independent of an optimized environment state. The achievable Gaussian term and a matching quantum expansion below infidelity one half were established recently. We prove matching upper bounds for every fixed infidelity, including private communication, with the displayed remainder. The proof bounds one code's average performance across all loss patterns of a given size; binomial fluctuations then determine the Gaussian correction. It combines tests of correct and secret communication with tensor-product averaging and a classical polynomial identity. Arbitrary mixed encoders and collective decoders are allowed. Requiring the private error bound for every message preserves the Gaussian term. Fixing the ideal environment state to the actual marginal instead changes the quantile to $Φ^{-1}(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon})$. Thus the precise privacy criterion affects communication at second order.

papers.abstract: The characterization of the quantum critical properties of genuine non-Hermitian many-body systems remains ambiguous as neither the state considered nor the definition of expectation values is unique. papers.abstract: Designing robust control protocols for multipartite entanglement is a central challenge for quantum technologies. We introduce a measurement-free collision-model protocol for preparing symmetric Dicke states |Dn(m)〉 using excitation-preserving partial-SWAP interactions between two qubit registers an…

papers.title: Linking quantum state texture to the fully entangled fraction in fixed-basis settings via Petz-Rényi relative entropy
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the quantum state texture (QST) measure based on the Petz-Rényi relative entropy and the fully entangled fraction (FEF). For two-qubit Werner states, we derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for faithful entanglement formulated in terms of QST. Simila…

papers.title: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in a $(2+1)$-dimensional transverse-field Ising model under decoherence
papers.abstract: Decoherence in many-body quantum systems can give rise to intrinsically mixed-state phases and phase transitions beyond the pure-state paradigm. Here we study the (2+1)D transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) subject to a strongly ℤ2-symmetric decoherence channel, with a focus on strong-to-weak spontan…

papers.title: Optimality of trine states for two-copy discrimination
papers.abstract: This work establishes that almost every pure state of a quantum system is uniquely determined by two overlapping reduced density matrices. It has potential applications for quantum state tomography and entanglement certification, where access to global measurements is often limited.

papers.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
papers.abstract: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.

papers.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
papers.abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.

papers.title: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
papers.abstract: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $ρ_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_ρ$ ebits per pair. We show that this cost is robust under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. For every $R>S(A|B)_ρ$, a single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on $ρ_{AB}$ and $R$, merges every weakly almost i.i.d. source along $ρ_{AB}$ with vanishing error. The net entanglement cost is at most $nR$ ebits for all sufficiently large blocklengths $n$. This guarantee also covers the Wasserstein and Mazzola--Sutter--Renner subclasses. Each class contains the exact i.i.d. source, so $S(A|B)_ρ$ is optimal for universal merging within each class. More generally, the same protocols achieve vanishing error whenever the two-pair marginal of the permutation-averaged source converges in trace norm to $ρ_{AB}^{\otimes 2}$.

papers.title: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments with an AI Agent
papers.abstract: Recent advances in AI-assisted theoretical research suggest that AI agents can contribute to research-level problems. Whether they can also advance experimental research by conducting experiments, analyzing the results, and proposing better experimental designs remains an open question. To address this question, we build a simulated quantum optics laboratory and integrate it with an AI agent in QuOptLab. The laboratory includes optical instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, enabling the agent to carry out and iteratively refine experiments. We consider two complementary tasks: thin-film thickness measurement in free-space optics and edge-coupler design in integrated photonics. In the thin-film thickness measurement task, the agent repeatedly analyzes measurement results and revises its measurement method, including calibration and data analysis, reducing thickness-estimation error from 7.13 to 0.066~nm$^2$ over six epochs in a classical-interference run. For edge-coupler design, the agent iteratively proposes structural modifications, evaluates the resulting coupling performance, and uses the feedback to guide subsequent revisions, increasing simulated coupling efficiency from 85.81% to 91.98%.

papers.title: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes
papers.abstract: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes. In every known positive construction the certificate is accompanied by a non-Clifford logical gate, leaving open whether a CSS family can satisfy these conditions to arbitrarily high order while admitting no such gate. We answer this question for the class of symmetric spectral CSS codes $Q(A)=CSS(C(A),C(A))$ built from character evaluation on a finite abelian group $G$ with $\exp(G)\mid p-1$, $p\geq 5$ prime. The mechanism is the identity \[C(A)^\perp * C(A)^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^G,\] which we call Schur saturation of the dual code. It follows from the CSS self-orthogonality condition $A\cap(-A)=\varnothing$ and annihilates every local polynomial phase of degree $\geq 3$. The complete gate-group classification $S^{CSS}_{\leq p-1}(A)=C(A)^\perp \oplus C(Stab(A))$ shows that every strictly CSS-preserving local-diagonal transversal gate lies at level $\leq 2$ of the Clifford hierarchy, a structural bound we call the Clifford ceiling. The criterion extends to arbitrary CSS pairs satisfying $C_Z^\perp * C_Z^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^n$; the LDPC instance $[[58,16,3]]_5$ is verified computationally. The false-positive character of the orthogonality certificates is sharpest in the Boolean toric family: these codes satisfy $\ell$-orthogonality for $\ell\leq p-2$, yet the non-Clifford sector collapses to zero. The flagship instance $[[64,56,3]]_5$ encodes $56$ logical ququints at rate $R=0.875$ with distance-$3$ protection, passes every orthogonality screening test, and yet admits no local-diagonal non-Clifford gate of any degree. The unique non-Pauli survivor is the uniform quadratic drive $Q_u$, fault-tolerant, logically nontrivial, and Clifford at level $2$, carrying no magic-state resource.

papers.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
papers.abstract: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Under the specified Lindblad conditions, local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization imply that an n-atom connected contribution to the root optical coherence is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. Consequently, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom connected clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions. Direct finite-cluster calculations confirm the predicted lowest allowed orders, while an illustrative Maxwell-propagation calculation shows that triplet contributions can partially oppose pair-induced polarization rotation. Our results establish a rigorous connection between optical perturbation order and the connected many-body sectors that can contribute to it.

papers.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

papers.title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
papers.abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.

papers.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
papers.abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

papers.title: Self-guided estimation of the stabilizer fidelity with single-copy Pauli measurements
papers.abstract: The stabilizer fidelity quantifies the non-stabilizerness of pure states, but it is hard to estimate because it requires optimizing over $2^{O(n^2)}$ stabilizer states for $n$ qubits. Here, we propose a self-guided estimation protocol for the stabilizer fidelity of an unknown state, pure or mixed, which requires only Pauli measurements on single copies. The protocol moves through the graph of neighboring stabilizer states, obtains the fidelities of a whole stabilizer basis from a single direct fidelity estimation, and reuses previous outcomes, which also provide a restart point that mitigates the barren plateau of a random start. In addition, it certifies the global optimum when the lower confidence bound of the estimated fidelity exceeds $\cos^2(π/8)$. In numerical simulations of up to 14 qubits, the protocol reached the optimum in all runs, with the number of iterations remaining small and increasing only slightly with $n$.

papers.title: Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
papers.abstract: Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals $γ+\frac{1-γ}{d}$ for transmission probabilities $0<γ\le \frac{1}{2}$ and logical dimension $d$. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.

papers.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
papers.abstract: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

papers.title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
papers.abstract: The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.

papers.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Ideal optical flux lattices
papers.abstract: The realization of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states in cold atomic gases is a long-standing goal in quantum simulation. Established approaches, including rapidly rotating gases and tight-binding lattices, are often hampered by low interaction energies and small many-body energy gaps. While optic…

papers.title: Numerical study of boson mixtures with multicomponent continuous matrix product states
papers.abstract: The continuous matrix product state (cMPS) ansatz is a promising numerical tool for studying quantum many-body systems in continuous space. Although it provides a clean framework that allows one to directly simulate continuous systems, the optimization of cMPS is known to be a very challenging task,…

papers.title: Network nonlocality with separable measurements
papers.abstract: Quantum correlations in networks with independent sources have revealed novel forms of nonclassical behavior. While entanglement in the sources is a necessary ingredient, the role played by entanglement in the measurements remains largely unexplored. In particular, all existing demonstrations of ful…

papers.title: Short-time initial correlations in nonequilibrium Green functions
papers.abstract: Within the Kadanoff-Baym equation, we propose an initial condition for simulating a many-body quantum system that has been disturbed from its steady state by a sudden event. The correlations that exist before the disturbance contribute to the system’s evolution during the initial stage, which extend…

papers.title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials. Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.

papers.title: Positive-partial-transpose structure of completely entangled subspaces and their complements
papers.abstract: A completely entangled subspace (CES) contains no product vectors, so every state supported on it is entangled. Whether such a subspace can support states with positive partial transpose (PPT) is a more subtle question. The normalized projector onto a CES may be NPT even if there exist PPT states supported on the CES. We investigate this distinction using a semidefinite criterion that optimizes the smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue over all supported density operators. For two- qutrit states supported on CESs, this leads to a complete characterization: a CES supports PPT states exactly when it is four-dimensional and related by invertible local transformations to the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We also establish restrictions on PPT states whose ranges contain only vectors of Schmidt rank at least three, ruling out their existence in $3\otimes n$, $4\otimes4$, and $4\otimes5$, and showing that any such state in $4\otimes6$ must have rank eight. An interesting structure emerges when two orthogonal completely entangled subspaces together span the full Hilbert space, which we term \textit{complementary CESs}. Explicit constructions in $3\otimes4$ demonstrate that both subspaces can support PPT entanglement even when their normalized projectors are NPT. In $4\otimes4$, we construct a complementary pair whose normalized projectors are themselves PPT entangled. These constructions offer an alternative route to obtaining PPT entangled states, beyond the familiar approach based on UPB complements.

papers.title: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response
papers.abstract: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol requires no time reversal, no ancilla, no double copy, and no weak measurement: a unitary string pulse, forward many-body evolution, and a single local readout suffice. An average over a complete basis of pulse generators yields the OTOC exactly. We further show that the measurement can be made sparse by restricting the pulses to a fixed operator weight, which turns the truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter: the deterministic bias can be computed before the experiment and cleanly separated from the statistical sampling variance. For Gaussian states, the finite-weight response is exactly proportional to the full OTOC after a known combinatorial rescaling. For quantum chaotic systems, the typical residual is suppressed as a power law in the sector size. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm these predictions.

papers.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
papers.abstract: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.

papers.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent
papers.abstract: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches between human players and an adaptive bot.

papers.title: Generalized Bloch Oscillations of Doublon Defect in One-dimensional Antiferromagnetic Atomic Spin Chain under Linear and Quadratic Magnetic Gradients
papers.abstract: We investigate generalized Bloch oscillations of a single doublon defect in a one-dimensional antiferromagnetic $t$-$J_{\rm{z}}$ chain subjected to linear and quadratic magnetic field gradients. By mapping the spin-charge coupled many-body dynamics onto an effective single-particle model, we reveal how the Néel background mediates parity-dependent coupling between the defect and the external fields. The linear gradient induces a staggered potential that splits the Wannier-Stark ladder into two intertwined subladders, producing a characteristic beating pattern in the center-of-mass motion with a subband offset accurately captured by third-order perturbation theory. The quadratic gradient generates sublattice-dependent tilts that shear the ladder into a scissor-like profile, yielding site-dependent beating periods that encode the nonlocal spatial averaging of the defect wave function. When both gradients coexist, their interplay is fundamentally nonadditive: the quadratic gradient breaks the two-site periodicity that forbids second-order linear responses, unlocking a dominant cross-coupling proportional to $B_{\rm{z,1}}B_{\rm{z,2}}$. This leaves distinct fingerprints on the Bloch-oscillation spectrum---a rigid baseline hift of the fundamental doublet and asymmetric broadening of the first harmonic. These predictions are quantitatively corroborated by exact many-body simulations of the real-time density evolution and center-of-mass dynamics. Our work establishes a gradient-induced unlocking mechanism for multi-gradient defect spectroscopy in quantum magnets, offering a framework for probing parity-protected selection rules and their controlled breaking via generalized Bloch oscillations in tunable quantum simulators.

papers.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
papers.abstract: We study how observed many-body system size affects the number of state copies needed to estimate a zero-temperature first-order transition point. The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size. For error $ε$ and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants $0<c_0<C$ and $c_1>0$ such that, at inverse temperature $β=c_1/ε$, restricting side lengths to $L\le c_0/ε$ requires $\exp(Ω(1/ε))$ copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements. Allowing $L\le C/ε$ permits $O(\log^2(1/ε))$ copies and $O(ε^{-3})$ total spins, using local measurements and polynomial classical postprocessing. The minimax expected total spin count is $Θ(ε^{-3})$ uniformly for $β\ge c_1/ε$. At fixed positive temperature it is $Θ_β(ε^{-2})$, attained from one- and eight-site Gibbs states followed by exponential classical computation. For ground-state copies it is $Θ(ε^{-3})$. The lower bound uses a three-state ferromagnet whose boundary suppresses the sector carrying transition information. A spanning-forest argument and edge-boundary counting control its Gibbs weight uniformly over fields and allowed sizes, and a trace-distance hybrid argument handles adaptive learners with quantum memory. The upper bound combines finite-volume free-energy estimates, concavity and local order-parameter measurements.

papers.title: Stopping-Time Leakage in Blind Quantum Delegation
papers.abstract: Blind quantum computation lets a client delegate a computation while hiding it from the server, up to a declared leakage. Its security definitions cover a single round. A variational quantum algorithm, however, delegates many rounds, and its classical optimizer decides from private data when to stop. We study what the resulting round count tells an honest-but-curious server. For protocols with one-time-padded transcripts and fresh randomness in every round, we prove that the server's best distinguishing advantage over the whole sequence equals the total-variation distance between the stopping-time distributions, so the round count is the only residual channel in this model. We also show that soundness composes as $δ\,\mathbb{E}[T]$ under adaptive stopping, given a conditional per-round soundness property that composably secure verifiable protocols provide. In simulated delegated eigensolvers for the transverse-field Ising chain, the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz ratio measured in iterations 5 to 15 predicts the noiseless stopping round with a leave-one-out error of 1.7 iterations, compared with 10.3 for a constant predictor. Across 14 configurations that differ in optimizer, stopping rule, initialization, system size, shot budget and problem family, the leakage is significant in 12 and ranges from 0.14 to 1.68 bits, and a maximum-entropy bound estimated on held-out sessions lies above it in all of them. For defense, we show that any mechanism acting after the stopping decision can only add rounds, and that differentially private padding costs the full adjacency radius. A fixed public iteration budget removes the channel completely; set at the median run length, it costs 10% of the remaining energy gap. A differentially private stopping rule based on AboveThreshold protects every pair of instances, but it must often stop too early, which makes it costly.

papers.title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
papers.abstract: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $γ$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-γ)γ^{γ/(1-γ)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and, for every $0<γ<1$, strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint. The bounds provide quantitative limits for adaptive communication through relaxing qubits and show how a sector simulation can remain useful beyond channels whose resource entanglement is known exactly.

papers.title: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes
papers.abstract: Can a joint measurement reveal nonclassical behaviour in independently prepared systems that share no entanglement? We study network contextuality by extending the two-qubit test of bi-contextuality [G. Ruffolo et al., arXiv:2507.08461 (2025)] to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. In one laboratory, an observer measures the systems individually or jointly performs two compatible global measurements constructed from them. The individual probabilities constrain the possible classical correlations at each source. For our preparations, every noncontextual model with outcome-deterministic and source-independent assignments predicts a nonzero average product of the two global outcomes. The joint quantum measurement gives zero. We construct explicit product states realizing this contradiction for $N=d$ independent sources, each preparing one $d$-dimensional system, with $2\leq d\leq9$. We derive an inequality in observed probabilities, prove its single-source bounds are exact for these preparations, and give sufficient thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise. For this family of preparations the dimension range is sharp: for every $d\geq10$ the individual probabilities admit a zero assigned average, so the certificate fails. The same data admit a noncontextual explanation when source independence is relaxed.

papers.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
papers.abstract: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.

papers.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
papers.abstract: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.

papers.title: Compact and Long-Term Stable Polarization Entangled Photon-Pair Source
papers.abstract: We present a robust, compact polarization-entangled photon-pair source based on bulk optics that achieves long-term stability, a spectral pair generation rate of $4.24 \times 10^6$ pairs s$^{-1}$ mW$^{-1}$ nm$^{-1}$ constant for pump powers up to 700 mW, an intrinsic heralding efficiency of 59.8% , and a polarization contrast visibility of 99.6%. The source is mechanically designed for vibrational robustness, employing an engineered base plate and a reduced optical layout for less alignment sensitivity and complexity. It operates at telecom wavelengths in C-band with a typical type-0 SPDC spectral output of 70 nm width. We demonstrate its integration into a deployed entanglement-based QKD system that bridges the gap between laboratory prototypes and practical quantum communication hardware.

papers.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.

papers.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
papers.abstract: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU. We further extend our method to systems with large spin baths that lie beyond the reach of exact methods. Our approach thus offers a scalable and systematically improvable route to accurately simulate the decoherence dynamics of sensors in realistic spin environments.

papers.title: Non-Abelian Twist Defects in Bivariate Bicycle Codes
papers.abstract: Bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity-check codes combine efficient quantum storage with a rich Abelian anyon structure, providing a compelling platform for exploring the interplay between quantum error correction and topological order. A central challenge is how to realize domain walls that host non-Abelian twist defects at their endpoints. Here we explicitly construct electric-magnetic duality walls for arbitrary bivariate bicycle codes with finite anyon content using composite, interblock, and patch checks. These checks remove the unwanted local modes while preserving charge conversion, ensuring that topologically contractible closed ribbons act trivially on encoded states. For each fixed code, check weights and interaction ranges remain bounded independently of wall length. The wall endpoints have quantum dimension $2^{Q/2}$, where $Q$ counts the independent generators in each electric or magnetic charge space. As an application, we illustrate measurement-only braiding for $Q=3$ under the correspondence between measurements and defect transport. Our construction provides a valuable basis for exploring non-Abelian defect physics and developing logical operations in quantum low-density parity-check codes with Abelian topological order in future.

papers.title: Sharp Purity Based Entropy Bounds and Machine Learning Assisted Entropy Estimation
papers.abstract: Purity quantifies quantum-state mixedness, motivating the study of its role in controlling entropy variations. A sharp purity-based continuity bound is established for the von Neumann entropy of qubit states. The bound is attainable for every admissible purity difference and strictly improves the existing purity bound. In higher dimensions, an explicit sharp bound is derived within the family of pure states mixed with the maximally mixed state. Further continuity estimates are obtained for conditional entropy, quantum mutual information, quantum conditional mutual information, and squashed entanglement within specified bipartite and tripartite families. An application to machine learning assisted qubit entropy estimation illustrates how the sharp bound converts purity estimation errors into rigorous entropy error bounds.

papers.title: Phase-dependent atomicity and PPT edge states for cyclic-sign covariant qutrit maps
papers.abstract: Decomposable positive maps cannot detect entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT). We obtain a necessary and sufficient criterion for decomposability in the entire seven-real-parameter class of Hermiticity-preserving cyclic-sign covariant maps on $M_3$. The criterion reduces to a one-variable inequality and, for positive maps in this class, characterizes indecomposability exactly. We apply it to a phase-dependent family obtained by adding a completely positive map to the Choi map. Every map in this family is positive, and we find the exact phase-dependent threshold for indecomposability and atomicity. At three phase values, the maps remain indecomposable for every finite deformation strength. Each indecomposable map gives an indecomposable entanglement witness through its Choi matrix. We construct PPT edge states of birank $(5,5)$ detected by these witnesses throughout the indecomposable region.

papers.title: Subquantum Pilot-Wave System Theory: Structural and Amplitude Nonequilibrium under Source Fields
papers.abstract: A source in the Schrodinger equation changes the norm of the guiding wave, apparently conflicting with the conservation of probability. In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Distant Bell States via Measured Spin Chain Dynamics
papers.abstract: Preparing distant qubits in Bell states is a core requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation. The nonequilibrium unitary dynamics of spin chains have been envisaged as a convenient quantum channel for intra-chip communications. Typically it establishes mixed entangled states between its remote ends, to be purified by entanglement distillation after several uses of the channel to obtain Bell states. Here we show how the establishment of entanglement via spin chain dynamics can be (a) sped up and (b) made to yield a pure entangled state after a single usage of the channel, which is upgradable to a Bell-state without the complexity of purification. To this end, we intersperse unitary evolution for some period with measurements on intermediary spins. We explore two different measurements: a measurement that post-selects for a ground state; and local measurements in the computational basis. We illustrate the mechanism with qubits coupled to the ends of a 1D $XY$ spin chain.

papers.title: Foliated surface codes for optimal skip-gate leakage correction
papers.abstract: Skip-gate leakage --- such as atom loss in neutral-atom arrays or trapped ions, or photon loss in superconducting dual-rail qubits --- takes a qubit out of its computational subspace and removes subsequent gates acting on it. If leakage is only detectable end-of-the-line at qubit measurement, error correction circuits must be designed to periodically measure all qubits, as in SWAP-based circuits and foliation. We show that the best SWAP-based surface code, although optimal against space-like skip-gate leakage errors, is suboptimal against time-like leakage errors. By optimal, we mean that the code corrects as many leakage errors as it can detect. Remarkably, we find that the foliated surface code is optimal against both space- and time-like error configurations. We support our findings with numerical simulations. Under two-qubit gate leakage with probability 0.5%, foliation suppresses time-like errors in a distance-4 rotated stability experiment by 1380(50) per two added rounds, compared to 63(1) for the best SWAP-based circuit. In memory, the two are comparable. Under an experimentally motivated neutral-atom noise model, we find that foliation outperforms SWAP-based circuits in stability for both rotated and unrotated code geometries. This holds true for a parameter sweep that takes the neutral-atom noise model from being dominated by computational errors to atom loss. Interestingly, a SWAP-based circuit for unrotated code memory performs best when computational noise dominates over loss. Our work motivates co-designing error correction circuits with logical operations: preferring foliation when time-like errors dominate and SWAP-based circuits when space-like errors dominate.

papers.title: State-selective dynamical freezing in driven Rydberg atom chains
papers.abstract: Dynamical freezing, the near-complete suppression of dynamics at special drive frequencies, offers a route to mitigating Floquet heating in periodically driven quantum systems. In interacting systems, however, the energy cost of each transition depends on the many-body configuration, so that the freezing condition itself becomes state dependent. We study this dependence in periodically driven Rydberg atom chains under single- and bi-frequency driving. Using Floquet perturbation theory, we show that each spin flip is characterised by a single interference amplitude set by its local interaction shift, and that a state freezes only where the amplitudes of all its available flips vanish simultaneously. This picture accounts quantitatively for the shift and proliferation of freezing frequencies with interatomic spacing and for the response of entire families of initial states, which are sorted by a single local motif. Freezing is strong only within a window of spacings bounded by interaction tails on one side and nearest-neighbour excitation facilitation on the other, outside of which the advantage of bi-frequency driving is lost. In the regime of large detuning amplitude, where freezing points are numerous and the perturbative description is controlled, this window leaves almost no room for the PXP limit.

papers.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus.
