papers.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry

papers.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
papers.abstract: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.

papers.title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schrödinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the Schrödinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

papers.title: Non-archimedean generalisations of the Kuznetsov formulas
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop non-archimedean analogues of the Petersson-Kuznetsov formulas. Specifically, choosing a particular test function on either the geometric or spectral side of the formula, one may express the other side in terms of integral transforms. Such transforms involve representation theoretic Bessel functions attached to irreducible unitary admissible representations of $\text{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate. For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $κ$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $κ<0$. The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

papers.title: Boundary Observability for a Class of Degenerate Kolmogorov-Type Equations in a Cylindrical Domain
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the boundary observability for a class of multi-dimensional degenerate Kolmogorov-type kinetic equations in a cylindrical domain $Ω= \mathbb{T}_{x_1} \times (0,1)_{x_2}$. The model features a horizontal drift term $x_2^γ\partial_{x_1} \varphi$ coupled with a boundary-degenerate diffusion operator $\partial_{x_2}(x_2^α\partial_{x_2} \varphi)$ acting solely on the velocity variable, where $γ= 1$ and $α\in (0,1)$. By leveraging the structural advantages of the cylindrical domain, we establish an analytical framework based on the method of separation of variables. Crucial Carleman estimates tailored to the degenerate dual operator are derived to capture the subtle dissipation effects under the influence of the transport term. Consequently, by virtue of a uniform a priori estimate, we establish the quantitative boundary observability inequality for the state function.

papers.title: A Garnett--Jones estimate for matrix weights
papers.abstract: For an \(N\times N\) matrix \(A_p\) weight \(W\) on an averaging basis, set \(M_p=\max\{1,p-1\}\), \(1\leq p<\infty\). At rate \(1/M_p\), the operator-norm exponential moment of \(\log W\) centered on each basis set is bounded by \(2[W]_{\mathbf A_p}^{1/M_p}\). With scalar Garnett--Jones constant \(G\), the BMO distance from \(\log W\) to bounded Hermitian functions is at most \((2N^2-N)GM_p\), uniformly in the characteristic. Power weights on intervals show the sharp order in \(p\). Conversely, a uniform distance bound for scalar \(A_2\) logarithms gives the scalar property with the same constant. Under a uniform small-BMO condition this is equivalent to scalar \(A_2\) decomposition. The estimates apply to cubes and axis-parallel rectangles on \(\R^d\) and \(\T^d\). For rectangles with \(d>1\), the scalar quadratic estimate bounds the distance by \(\sqrt{2N^2-N}\,C_d M_p\), where \(C_d\) depends only on \(d\). The rectangular BMO distance is comparable to the critical exponential scale.

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.abstract: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Doğan and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

papers.title: Cyclic polynomials in mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type spaces
papers.abstract: For $\boldsymbolα=(α_1,α_2,α_3)\in\mathbb R^3$, we investigate cyclic polynomials in the mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type space $\mathscr{D}_{\boldsymbolα}$ of holomorphic functions $f(z_1,z_2)=\sum_{m,n\geq0}a_{m,n}z_1^mz_2^n$ on the unit bidisk satisfying $$ \sum_{m,n\geq0}|a_{m,n}|^2 (m+1)^{α_1}(n+1)^{α_2} (m+n+1)^{α_3}<\infty. $$ We give a complete characterization of cyclic polynomials in terms of their zero sets and the parameters $α_1,α_2,α_3$. Our results extend previously known characterizations for anisotropic and total-degree Dirichlet-type spaces on the unit bidisk.

papers.title: Entire function related to shift and difference operator
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uniqueness problems of entire functions involving difference operators. First, we examine the case where $f-a$, $Δ_c^n f-b$, and $Δ_c^{n+2}f-b$ share $0$ CM (counting multiplicities), where $a$ and $b$ are two entire small functions of $f$ such that $Δ_c^m a \equiv 0$ ($1 \le m \le n$), and $b$ is $c$-periodic. As a consequence, we establish two main results, one of which resolves a conjecture posed by Farissi et al. \cite{FLBA1}. Second, we obtain a uniqueness theorem for an entire function $f(z)$ when $f(z)$, $f(z+c)$, and $Δ_c f(z)$ share a single value, thereby improving and generalizing the corresponding result of Farissi et al. \cite{FLA1} by removing the growth restriction on the order of $f$. Third, we establish uniqueness results for $f(z)$ when $f(z)$ and $Δ_c^k f(z)$ share a value, which improve and generalize the findings of Chen et al. \cite{CCL2} and Huang and Zhang \cite{HZ1}. Finally, we provide several examples to demonstrate that our results are best possible in certain senses.

papers.title: Uniqueness Sequences in the Bargmann-Fock Space
papers.abstract: We show that a locally finite sequence with prescribed multiplicities is a uniqueness sequence in the Bargmann-Fock space if and only if a variational supremum involving Jensen potentials and Gaussian relative entropy is infinite. The proof combines exact subharmonic duality with holomorphic realization at the original Gaussian weight. Restricting the supremum to radial tests yields a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for locally finite unions of pairwise disjoint regular rotation orbits satisfying a bounded-overlap condition. For a planar lattice containing the origin and having fundamental area $π$, changing only the arguments of its nonzero points yields a uniqueness sequence provided that the resulting points are pairwise distinct. In particular, independently and uniformly rotating the nonzero points of the critical square lattice yields an almost surely complete system of coherent states. Finally, we reduce the general criterion to countably many polynomial tests and give finite approximations to each test score with explicit error bounds.

papers.title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
papers.abstract: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact Kähler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact Kähler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).

papers.title: A formula to construct all elements of finite order in Riordan matrix groups
papers.abstract: We characterize the elements of finite order in the Riordan group over the complex field by providing explicit conditions on their entries. Our main result generalizes a previous characterization of involutions to arbitrary finite orders and gives a constructive procedure to determine all Riordan matrices of a prescribed finite order from a suitable choice of parameters. The proof relies on an inductive analysis of the principal submatrices. We further derive consequences for the Lagrange subgroup and the group of formal power series under composition, obtaining a characterization of finite-order series and a constructive description of the solutions to associated functional equations.

papers.title: Simultaneous ruin probabilities for Brownian risks with a deterministic splitting time
papers.abstract: We consider two Brownian risk processes which coincide up to a fixed time and subsequently evolve with correlated increments. For a finite time horizon after the split, we derive the exact asymptotics of their simultaneous ruin probability as the initial reserves tend to infinity proportionally. The terminal correlation separates the two asymptotic regimes for the ratio to the joint tail at the terminal time. If both coordinates contribute to the leading Gaussian tail, the ratio is a bivariate Piterbarg-type constant, for which we give an integral representation and explicit bounds. In the remaining regimes the ratio equals two, with a Gaussian factor in the endpoint tail at the transition. We also obtain asymptotics on intervals of length of order $u^{-2}$ near the terminal time and an exponential limit law for the first simultaneous ruin time, conditional on ruin by the horizon.

papers.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
papers.abstract: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract: For every finite subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincaré pairing on $S^3/Γ$. In particular, $Γ$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

papers.title: Parameter selection procedures for model reduction of a parameterized wave propagation in damaged material
papers.abstract: In this work, we consider a parameterized version of the classical wave equation that models wave propagation in damaged material. We apply model order reduction to the wave equation using a reduced basis method with the POD-Greedy algorithm. The success of the model order reduction highly depends on the parameter set used in the POD-Greedy algorithm. While a larger parameter set leads to more insight on the behavior of the full order model, it also prolongs the reduction process in the offline phase for constructing the reduced basis. Therefore, subsampling strategies based on Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method, pivoted QR decomposition and Polytope Division Method are applied.

papers.title: Induced Independence Levels and Signed Enumeration in Powers of Cycles
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $α(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $α(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. The resulting Boolean-interval partition gives exact enumeration by subset cardinality. We also prove reconstruction of partially deleted forward neighborhoods and determine the support, signs, and multiplicities of the corresponding upper Möbius transform. For cycle squares we develop a complementary greedy-chain method for signed enumeration, with a five-transition classification and explicit staircase and two-gap cancellation identities.

papers.title: Rigidity of submanifolds under extrinsic curvature pinching
papers.abstract: We investigate the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds whose curvature operator is bounded below by a nonnegative constant, under pointwise pinching conditions involving the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to many earlier results, we allow equality in these conditions without imposing additional assumptions on the mean curvature or restricting the fundamental group of the submanifold. Allowing equality reveals geometric and topological phenomena excluded by strict pinching. We establish classification theorems in all dimensions $n\geq4$, describing the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of such submanifolds. Our results also provide substantial information about the extrinsic geometry of the immersions, including precise conclusions concerning relative nullity, Dupin principal normals, and total geodesicity. As applications, we derive rigidity and sphere theorems for submanifolds of space forms and construct families of examples showing that the pinching conditions do not, in general, imply extrinsic rigidity. These results extend and refine several known rigidity theorems by providing a classification of the equality cases in a general ambient setting.

papers.title: The Brownian Lévy transformation is exact
papers.abstract: We prove that the Lévy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.

papers.title: A Finite Automaton Translating Geometric Addresses into Dynamical Itineraries on the Basilica
papers.abstract: Fractals are generally known for their self-similarity and repeating patterns. One way to produce fractals is via the dynamics of functions from the extended complex plane to itself. These fractals are known as Julia sets. In this paper, we explore how methods from symbolic dynamics and computation theory can be used to describe where points on the basilica Julia set might be located depending on their dynamical orbit under the polynomial function $f(z)=z^2-1$.

papers.title: $μ$MPC: Microsecond-Scale Nonlinear and World Model Control from Edge to GPU via Koopman-Linearized Precompilation
papers.abstract: We present $μ$MPC, a fast model predictive control (MPC) framework that reduces online computation using learned Koopman-linearized dynamics. By precomputing finite-horizon control-to-output maps, $μ$MPC eliminates lifted-state trajectories, yielding an action-only Koopman-Compiled QP (KC-QP) with $Hn_u$ decision variables, independent of lifted dimension. A fixed, precomputed primal operator enables efficient primal-dual iterations using only matrix-vector products and projections, accommodating changing goals and constraints without refactorization. This efficiency also enables control-aware dynamics learning through differentiable KC-QPs in the training loop and batched DAgger-style data aggregation. $μ$MPC achieves solve times as low as $23μ$s on a desktop CPU and 24 ms onboard a 168 MHz Crazyflie microcontroller. It scales to 4096D quadruped control in under 5 ms, visual planning with 2048D world models in 0.4 ms, and collision-aware planning for 200 quadrotors at over 30 Hz on the GPU. Across these benchmarks, $μ$MPC achieves up to $108\times$ faster constrained MPC and $1907\times$ faster visuomotor planning than competing methods.

papers.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
papers.abstract: Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories. Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem. Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that in a strong linearly distributive category every formal diagram commutes.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mariño conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: Sequential Portfolio Optimizer (SPO-CPU and SPO-GPU): C++ Interior-Point Solvers and Differentiable Layers for Quadratic Cone Programs
papers.abstract: Quadratic cone programs (QCPs) are a practical canonical form for convex optimization, including parametric portfolio problems that must be re-solved to high accuracy as market data change. We present Sequential Portfolio Optimizer (SPO), with SPO-CPU and SPO-GPU the C++ and CUDA realizations of the Clarabel homogeneous-embedding interior-point method. Clarabel is a registered trademark; SPO is our name for these implementations. Each exposes a forward optimizer and an in-solver differentiable layer. The Mehrotra algorithm is unchanged. The contribution is an implementation stack: a reduced two-block vector-Jacobian product with gradients in the original coordinates; a documented variant of the Chen--Goulart--Jones smoothing warm start, applied in equilibrated coordinates; and a GIL-free GPU batch architecture whose isolated throughput is at parity with a warm solver loop up to $B{=}16$. On an RTX A6000, subsequent solves of a $5000$-asset factor-model QP average $24$ ms on SPO-GPU, compared with $98$ ms on Clarabel.rs and $122$ ms on single-thread Gurobi; at $10{,}000$ assets the corresponding GPU time is $59$ ms against $439$ ms for one-thread Mosek. Clarabel.rs, SPO-CPU, and SPO-GPU agree pairwise to $2.2{\times}10^{-7}$ in relative objective on this family. Against a CVXPYLayers baseline driven by Clarabel, the GPU layer reproduces the solution and the return-gradient on a $5000$-asset factor QP/SOCP, while a subsequent forward-plus-backward step is $101$--$137\times$ faster at $5000$ assets (and $17$--$30\times$ at $1000$ assets). The smoothing warm start reduces QP rebalance iterations but can increase them on a large GPU second-order cone. Wall-clock rankings apply to the factor-model family only; an $18$-problem Maros--Mészáros subset is reported as a cross-check. We do not claim a speedup over CuClarabel, and the batch architecture is not a measured throughput improvement.

papers.title: A branching construction for nonlinear Hawkes processes - Application to a case of infinite inhibition
papers.abstract: This article aims at introducing a genealogical branching structure for a wide class of nonlinear Hawkes processes. This construction extends the well-known Poisson cluster decomposition for linear Hawkes processes to the nonlinear case. More precisely, we perform a past dependent pruning of a Crump-Mode-Jagers tree with immigration and obtain an explicit formula for the conditional intensity of the point measure charging the birth times of the individuals. This pruning can be interpreted as the spreading of a heritable mutation in the population, when the mutation rate depends on the past of the population. Changing the parameters of the underlying Crump-Mode-Jagers process, as well as those of the pruning, allows obtaining various intensity functions, including those of the nonlinear Hawkes processes, thus embedding the nonlinear Hawkes process in a larger family of past-dependent point processes. We thereby provide the first embedding of a genealogical structure within a nonlinear Hawkes process, and obtain as a byproduct a new coupling with an upperbounding linear Hawkes. We finally study the impact of adding periods of infinite inhibition after each event of a supercritical Hawkes process. In particular we show that depending on the existence of a delay for this infinite inhibition, the process can exhibit either linear or exponential growth of the number of events with time. We obtain explicit criteria for both behaviors depending on the reproduction function, the delay and the length of these inhibition periods.

papers.title: A consequence of the classical Lindelöf Hypothesis for the density of zeros of general Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: Supposing the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function we prove that the density hypothesis holds for Res>3/4 for a large class of Dirichlet series. The first result of similar type was reached by Gábor Halász and Paul Turán in 1969.

papers.title: Routing and Cache Retention for Multi-Turn LLM Inference: Theory and Implementation
papers.abstract: Multi-turn AI agents execute iterative loops of large language model (LLM) inference and external tool calls, transforming cluster serving into a dynamic resource-allocation problem where routing and key-value (KV) cache retention jointly govern prefix reuse across inter-turn delays. We formulate a fluid approximation of this system and show that optimal admission, routing, and eviction are governed by endpoint-specific shadow prices for computation and memory together with session continuation values. Building on this structure, we propose an asymptotically optimal buffer-reserve policy that absorbs stochastic fluctuations using a vanishing share of capacity. To handle asynchronous arrivals, delayed load reports, and engine-local memory management in production clusters, we translate these principles into a practical controller named PARK, which pairs online projected subgradient price updates and one-turn migration lookahead with a local KV retention index ranked by expected reuse value per byte-epoch. In real GPU cluster experiments serving a 197-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model on multi-turn software-engineering agent benchmarks (SWE and Terminal-Bench), PARK outperforms all five load-balancing and prefix-aware baselines across contrasting traffic regimes. On 16 H200 GPUs, PARK raises output throughput by $24.2\%$ over the strongest baseline ($336.9\%$ over round robin) on turn-intensive SWE trajectories and by $40.0\%$ over the strongest baseline ($63.3\%$ over round robin) on generation-intensive Terminal-Bench trajectories. Controlled single-replica ablations show that our retention index alone cuts prior-prefix token loss from $13.26\%$ to $2.17\%$ and increases throughput by $36.7\%$ over least-recently-used (LRU) eviction, while 128-GPU scale-up experiments sustain 50,789 to 67,363 output tokens/s across 16~replicas with prefix cache hit rates of $91.3\%$ to $97.4\%$.

papers.title: Tian-Yau-type metrics from K3 divisors with ADE contractions
papers.abstract: We construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler metrics on the complement of a smooth anti-canonical K3 divisor in a compact Kähler threefold, assuming that the normal bundle of the divisor is nef and big. Such a metric exists in every Kähler class whose exceptional periods are positive. We use a generalized Gibbons-Hawking ansatz to construct an approximate model on the normal bundle. When the normal bundle contracts an ADE configuration, this model combines an expanding Ricci-flat orbifold K3 metric with ALE metrics whose exceptional periods remain fixed. After improving the model by a finite iteration and transferring it to the divisor complement, we apply the Tian-Yau-Hein existence theorem.

papers.title: On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: Local models are used to model, étale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein. On one hand, this gives the analogous information for integral models of Shimura varieties for unramified unitary groups with parahoric level structure, and on the other hand also results in certain natural matrix equations defining non-Gorenstein singularities.

papers.title: Stable finiteness and combination theorems for Hughes-free embeddings
papers.abstract: We show that all group algebras of Higman's group and Deligne's group are stably finite. We also study when the Hughes-free embeddability property is closed under taking graphs of groups, and give a positive answer when the edge maps are retractions or injective on Abelianisations. As a consequence we obtain that fundamental groups of graphs of torsion-free Abelian groups, graph products of locally indicable Hughes-free embeddable groups, and fundamental groups of graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups are Hughes-free embeddable.

papers.title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
papers.abstract: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.

papers.title: Large deviations for integrated exponentials of Gaussian Volterra processes - application to variance options
papers.abstract: We prove small-time large deviations for the normalised time integral of the exponential of a Gaussian Volterra process, and complement it with a central limit theorem and moderate deviations. As an application, we obtain short-maturity asymptotics for out-of-the-money and at-the-money variance options in rough volatility models, as well as implied volatility expansions which we validate numerically.

papers.title: Pietsch's favourite problem on singular traces
papers.abstract: In 2023, A. Pietsch formulated twenty-seven open problems concerning traces on operator ideals. We give an affirmative answer to Problem 16, which Pietsch singled out as his personal favourite, by constructing a nonzero bounded singular spectral trace on the weak Weyl ideal over the class of all Banach spaces.

papers.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
papers.abstract: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

papers.title: A second-order relaxation system for a degenerate-parabolic quasilinear fourth-order rimming-flow equation with critical spectrum
papers.abstract: For a spectrally critical nonlinear degenerate-parabolic PDE of fourth-order, describing a capillary-driven fluid flow in a rotating cylinder, we propose a second-order relaxation system of parabolic-elliptic type. For positive initial data, we prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the relaxation system. Thereby, the lifespan of the approximate solutions turns out to be independent of the relaxation parameter. Moreover, we prove convergence of non-negative weak solutions of the relaxation system to weak solutions of the original equation on compact time intervals. We classify positive steady states of the relaxed system, prove a stability result yielding global strong solutions, and show that the long-time dynamics remain consistent under the relaxation limit.

papers.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
papers.abstract: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.

papers.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta-function: a local multiplicity test and long mixed moments
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that at least 71.274066\% of the nontrivial zeros of $ζ(s)$ are simple, and at least 85.368230% are distinct. The previous bounds were 19/27 $\approx$ 70.37%, due to Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek and to Bui and Heath-Brown (2013), and 84.77\%, due to Chirre, Gonçalves and de Laat (2020). The method combines the two classical approaches to simple zeros. Montgomery's pair correlation argument rests on a pointwise consequence of the explicit formula: at a zero of multiplicity $m\ge2$, a Dirichlet polynomial $J$ over prime powers of length $T^ψ$, $ψ<1$, is forced to have real part at most $-a<0$. The mollified derivative $ζ'(ρ)M(ρ)$ of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek vanishes there. Both facts are used at the same zero, in a single least-squares inequality. The new analytic input is the mixed moment $\sum_ρζ'(ρ)M(ρ)J(1-ρ)$ with $J$ much longer than the mollifier. We evaluate it under the Riemann Hypothesis alone; the long prime sum stays in the numerator and the mollifier variable is the modulus, so the barrier at $T^{1/2}$ does not arise. A second-order version of the argument gives $0.70736$. We show that no second-order certificate of this type can exceed $0.7073646063$, and pass this ceiling with fourth moments of short Dirichlet polynomials and with mixed moments against products of a bounded number of primes. All constants are certified in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

papers.title: Hall's condition between adjacent levels of the face lattice of the permutohedron
papers.abstract: Let $\OP$ be the poset of ordered set partitions of $[n]$, ordered by merging adjacent blocks; with a bottom element adjoined it is the face lattice of the permutohedron. Whether it has the Sperner property is open. We show that for every pair of adjacent levels, the smaller one can be matched into the larger one by parent--child pairs, except possibly for the pairs $(j,j+1)$ with $(28n-36)/39<j<(13n+5)/18$ (for small $n$ the window is slightly smaller still). This window has width about $n/234\approx0.0043\,n$. The largest level lies near $n/(2\ln2)\approx0.7213\,n$, which we prove using the law of the block sizes of a uniformly random ordered set partition of $[n]$, and for $n$ large it falls inside the window. Since the level sizes are log-concave, Hall's condition for all pairs would make $\OP$ Sperner. The proofs use explicit weights on the parent--child pairs; they reduce to a finite inequality between pairs of adjacent blocks. We explain why the simplest weights fail exactly at the boundary of a much larger window, and report computations supporting Hall's condition inside the window: exactly for $n\le14$, and by equalizing flows for every window pair with $n\le25$.

papers.title: Square-root comparison, Turnpike, and exact semidefinite feasibility
papers.abstract: Given positive integers $a_i,K$, put $S=\sum_{i=1}^k\sqrt{a_i}$. We construct a realizable Turnpike instance in which the minimum spacing of distinct distances and the smallest nonzero addition residual are both at most $|S-K|$ when $S\ne K$. With approximation oracles, one three-distance realizability query decides $S\le K$. For unordered lists of radical sums with nonnegative rational coefficients, a polynomial-time substitution by integers preserves every normalized ruler. We give the classical reduction of square-root comparison to exact semidefinite feasibility in both threshold directions. The comparison enters through numerical separation and marked sorting; the integer recoding needs no such comparison for unordered reconstruction.

papers.title: Viscosity solutions for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms
papers.abstract: We address global well-posedness for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms. This naturally results from establishing the comparison principle for viscosity solutions and existence via Perron's method. There are many earlier results for similar equations, and our work attempts to give a unified approach and improve upon some recent examples. There is a natural juxtaposition of earlier results in the usual framework of viscosity solutions which rely on a min-max structure, with some more recent implementations coming from the free boundary literature in which a min-max is not apparent initially, but does appear a posteriori due to certain rigid structural constraints. Here we give a presentation that combines ideas from both situations. The most important feature of the operators in our equations is what we call the global comparison property. This is combined with a natural local Lipschitz assumption on the operator defining the equation.

papers.title: Convergence of Residual-driven Adaptive Kernel-based Multilevel Approximation
papers.abstract: Kernel-based multilevel methods combine compactly supported radial basis functions with a residual correction scheme and are known to converge linearly in the number of levels. In this paper we study an adaptive version of the multilevel method, in which the interpolation on each level only uses those sites at which the residual of the preceding level exceeds a given threshold. Although this method has been proposed some time ago and converges in all numerical tests, a convergence proof has been missing so far. We close this gap. We derive an a priori error bound, an a posteriori error bound valid for arbitrary point selections, and extend the analysis to penalized least-squares approximation and to target functions outside the native space of the kernel. For a variant with an additional check-loop per level, we show convergence with the rate of the classical multilevel method. We illustrate our findings with three numerical examples.

papers.title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $σ\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(σ)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $σ$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.

papers.title: Existence of complete singular solutions of the Yamabe equation at prescribed points
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be smooth, connected and closed, with $n\ge3$, and let $P$ be a prescribed nonempty finite set. We characterize the conformal classes $[g]$ that admit a complete metric of positive constant scalar curvature on $M\setminus P$. Such a metric exists precisely when $Y(M,[g])>0$ and either $[g]$ is nonround or $|P|\ge2$. In a nonround positive conformal class, the metrics can be chosen with Fowler asymptotics and arbitrary fixed ratios of their small asymptotic neck sizes. As the neck sizes tend to zero, every sequence of these metrics has a subsequence converging smoothly away from the punctures to a smooth Yamabe minimizing metric. The construction allows degenerate Yamabe minimizers and arbitrary curvature jets at the prescribed points. For nonempty closed singular sets $Λ\subset M$ with empty interior, we also announce the same existence criterion with the additional requirement that the Bessel capacity $C_{1+2/n,n/2}(Λ)$ vanish.

papers.title: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface
papers.abstract: We study the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field pulls back to a nonuniform surface field. The cyclic longitudinal coordinate permits an exact transverse reduction. The ordinary helicoid in the same axial field shares the effective potential and the turning points, while the conformal metric increases the physical period at matched energy and longitudinal momentum. We classify the single- and double-well regimes and obtain the exact transverse periods in the two double-well sectors. The periods diverge logarithmically at the separatrix, with twice the leading coefficient above the barrier as below it. The zero-field limit allows transverse escape, and the weak-twist limit is locally free but nonuniform across the surface. Intrinsic quantization gives an exact weighted transverse eigenvalue problem. Fixed-momentum eigenvalues test the harmonic approximation in a central well and resolve the tunneling splittings in a double well.

papers.title: Nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct smooth nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase $(n-2)π/2$ for every $n\ge4$. Together with the nonquadratic example in dimension two and Warren's example in dimension three, our construction shows that the supercritical condition $|θ|>(n-2)π/2$ in the Bernstein theorem proved by Yuan is sharp in every dimension $n\ge2$.

papers.title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
papers.abstract: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by Götze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.

papers.title: Selecting $2 \times 2$ submatrices with optimally bounded inverses
papers.abstract: For a matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ ($n \ge k$) with orthonormal columns, the Goreinov--Tyrtyshnikov--Zamarashkin (GTZ) conjecture asserts that there exists a $k \times k$ submatrix $U_I$ with $\|U_I^{-1}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}$. The conjecture remains open for $3 \le k \le n - 3$. The existence of such a submatrix in the case $k = 2$ was proved for $n=4$ by Nesterenko (2023) and recently for general $n$ by Sengupta and Pautov (2026). In this paper, we give a short, elementary, constructive proof of a weighted strengthening of this result, which yields a single-pass streaming algorithm that selects a row pair satisfying the $\sqrt{n}$ bound in $\mathcal O(n)$ operations and $\mathcal O(1)$ auxiliary memory. We further give an explicit matrix representation of all equality cases for $k = 2$ characterized by Nesterenko (2026) and use it to construct a single matrix family on which standard selection strategies (including global and local maximum-volume selection, Bischof--Stewart pivoted QR, column-pivoted QR, and LU with partial pivoting) simultaneously fail to attain the $\sqrt{n}$ bound.

papers.title: StePPO: Adaptive Step-Size Control for Initial-Value Problems Using Proximal Policy Optimisation
papers.abstract: ODE solvers are used to model, simulate, and analyse continuous-time systems found in many signal processing applications. Time integration of these initial-value problems is traditionally performed using adaptive embedded Runge--Kutta methods. For proper time-step selection, adaptive solvers accept or reject each candidate step according to a local error estimate. Their efficiency is therefore controlled by the rule that selects the next step size. Classical proportional--integral--derivative (PID) controllers are computationally inexpensive per decision and reliable, but their reactive design can lead to costly numerical solves near stiff transitions. We formulate step-size selection for parametrised IVPs as a Markov decision process and train a continuous-action policy using proximal policy optimisation. The policy processes its observation signals using a deep network while maintaining the embedded solver logic. We evaluate on a decay function, the Van der Pol system, and the Brusselator system at matched tolerances, and compare against a standard PID controller and a multi-scale DeepONet network. We find that the proposed learned policy remains within prescribed error tolerances while reducing the required number of solve steps by up to 60%, achieving a wall-clock time reduction of 58%, for both in- and out-of-distribution settings.

papers.title: On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties
papers.abstract: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five. Finally, we complete Ein's classification of smooth nondegenerate complex projective varieties with smooth projective dual. The list consists of smooth quadrics, the Segre varieties $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^m$ with $m\ge2$, the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$, and the spinor tenfold in $\mathbb P^{15}$.

papers.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
papers.abstract: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

papers.title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Decisions under uncertainty increasingly rest on fragmented evidence, such as samples from related but different populations, privacy-protected summary statistics, or complementary statistical descriptions of the same data. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) can fuse such evidence by constructing one ambiguity set per source and hedging against all distributions in the intersection of these sets. This fusion approach is less conservative than aggregating the sources into a single ambiguity set, but it is computationally demanding. Exact reformulations grow exponentially with the number of sources, and even deciding whether the intersection is nonempty is NP-hard. We show that fusion DRO admits an exact reformulation in which the ambiguity sets are coupled only through functional Lagrange multipliers. Restricting these multipliers to affine decision rules yields upper bounds that decompose across the ambiguity sets, are exact for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references, and provably dominate aggregation-based relaxations such as Minkowski sums and balls around mixtures. The approximations admit finite conic reformulations in important special cases and subgradient methods for weakly convex losses, which makes fusion DRO applicable to neural network training. In portfolio, newsvendor, and binary classification experiments, the affine approximation stays close to the exact value wherever the latter is computable, scales far better than exact methods, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample.

papers.title: The Monge Optimal Transport Barycenter Problem with Adaptive Features
papers.abstract: The data-driven Monge optimal transport barycenter problem seeks a map $y=T(x,z)$ that minimally perturbs an outcome $x$ while removing its statistical dependence on covariates $z$. Numerical implementations approximate the independence constraint through finite-dimensional test-function spaces, making the effectiveness of dependence removal sensitive to the choice of features. This article develops a procedure whereby the features themselves are optimized throughout the procedure. In particular, we adopt a feature space for $f$ consisting of Gaussian radial basis functions (RBFs) with adaptive individual centers and bandwidths. Synthetic experiments show that while fixed nonlinear RBF features can capture dependence structures that are poorly represented by linear features, adapting the RBF centers and bandwidths can further improve dependence removal within a limited feature space and achieve residual dependence comparable to that obtained with a larger fixed basis. We further extend the formulation to multidimensional covariates and evaluate its applicability to real-world problems, including removing age-related dependence in biomedical measurements and dependence on temperature and humidity in bike-sharing demand.

papers.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
papers.abstract: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $π$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $π$-ordered imaginarity. In this refined framework, free states are required to be real in the reference basis and to obey a prescribed permutation order $π$ for their diagonal populations. This theory thereby identifies two independent quantum resources: complex phases and population misordering, where the latter is inaccessible within the standard imaginarity resource theory. We characterize the structure of free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, define admissible $π$-ordered real operations, and examine their intersection with $π$-ordered incoherent operations. We further construct resource quantifiers for the $π$-ordered imaginarity based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness, and derive inequalities relating the robustness of $π$-ordered imaginarity and that of $π$-ordered coherence. The present framework generalizes the standard resource theory of imaginarity to incorporate population ordering and is naturally suited for thermodynamic settings such as quantum batteries.

papers.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

papers.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
papers.abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z$, the advantage is governed by $λ_X^2+λ_Y^2+λ_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

papers.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.

papers.title: Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^\varphi g+1$$ has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Brück's conjecture.

papers.title: Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem
papers.abstract: Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. In this paper, we construct a solution with a free boundary point of frequency 3.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
papers.abstract: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

papers.title: Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity. The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.

papers.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
papers.abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincaré maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.

papers.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers
papers.abstract: Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions. For a fixed positive semidefinite integral form on a box of radius $H$, with a linear term of coefficients $O(H)$, the algorithm computes all level counts simultaneously in $O(H^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit operations when $H=O(\sqrt m)$ and the facet offsets have $O(\log(2m))$ bits. A signed decomposition into orthogonal simplices gives this bound. For fullerenes we use deterministic $O(m^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work to construct an index of $O(m\log(2m))$ bits. With this index a rank costs $O(m\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work, uniformly in the rank. Two families of recuts let energy descent escape self-contacts in the slit polygon. The decoder then writes the graph from its selected period in $O(m)$ arithmetic word operations.

papers.title: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
papers.abstract: Exact state-preparation circuits are normally judged by how closely the measured output distribution reproduces the target. Using the ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph construction compiled into {Ry, X, CNOT}, we ask instead how much the accuracy of a probability-distribution loading depends on which of several logically equivalent compilations is executed. Two Gray-code realisations of the level-2 uniformly controlled rotation, A and B, differ only in the order of their CNOT controls: same unitary, same angles. On a three-qubit liquid-state NMR processor they do not perform identically. Across 700 runs over seven targets the A/B contrast is significant for 3 of them under Holm, with no fixed sign. Two further campaigns isolate the effect within one unit. Removing the circuit's identity-equivalent gates, which changes the executed schedule but not the unitary, affects the two realisations differently: a ladder x intervention interaction of +0.0625 (95% CI [+0.0306, +0.0944], paired p = 4.8e-4), reversing the sign of the A/B advantage. Across five acquisitions of this one logical circuit the contrast runs from +0.0395 to -0.0229. Not every compilation choice matters: commanding the two level-1 inverse rotations as 720 deg - theta rather than -theta, with the gate list unchanged, moves the mean fidelity by -0.0006 ([-0.0157, +0.0146]) on one target in one session. We offer the order and timing of the executed pulses as the hypothesis these observations favour, without identifying a mechanism. The metric does not certify coherences, and the measured correlators are inconsistent with any global depolarising description: on the uniform target, at a classical fidelity of 0.962, a two-body correlation of +0.217 appears where the target has none. Run-level data and code are deposited for every campaign run on our own unit; the pulse-level campaign is reported from summary tables.

papers.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

papers.title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions are common in applied optimization: parity checks, radar-code sidelobes, portfolio skewness and kurtosis, and marketing-channel synergies all yield cubic or quartic objectives. Quantum annealers and most Ising machines accept only quadratic objectives, and gate-based quantum processors build every higher-order term from two-qubit gates. Entropy quantum computing, realized in the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system, accepts polynomials of degree up to five with all-to-all coupling over binary, integer or simplex-constrained continuous variables. No user-supplied quadratization or circuit compilation is needed. We formulate four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic instances, run them on Dirac-3S with 30 samples each, and score every sample against a certified optimum or a classical best-known value. We also estimate their cost on quantum annealers, superconducting grids and trapped-ion registers under standard mappings. For the two densest instances, a portfolio with about 80,000 terms and a budget allocation with 360,000 terms, the quadratized problems need embeddings far beyond current annealers, over $10^5$ physical qubits for the portfolio alone, and one phase-separation layer costs over $10^6$ two-qubit gates before optimization. Dirac-3S ran all six natively and returned feasible, distinct solutions. All samples of the binary instances are single-flip local minima. The best portfolio sample lies within 0.32% of the best-known value and the best budget sample 15% above it, but no sample reached its reference. Classical solvers reach the references within minutes at these sizes, and random starts followed by a local polish reach comparable or better values, so the advantage established here is one of expressibility and mapping cost, not of solution quality. Whether it extends to time to solution at larger sizes remains open.

papers.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
papers.abstract: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.

papers.title: The singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
papers.abstract: We compute the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. We assume that the kernel of the Paneitz operator consists of the constants. In each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the Euler characteristic and the conical orders. We match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. A localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. For generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. Assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. If the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. At one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. On the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling
papers.abstract: Multistage stochastic programs (MSPs) with discrete decisions are hard to solve due to the curse of dimensionality, non-convex value functions, and scenario trees that grow exponentially with the horizon. We develop a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework for MSPs in which a neural network predicts scores for the part of the decision that drives the state transition. Under structural conditions that make this sub-decision enter the stage objective linearly, the network is trained on labels from offline single-scenario problems, using the Fenchel-Young loss with perturbed optimizers, which need only an optimization oracle. We apply the framework to repair scheduling in power networks under stochastic, time-varying component failures, with and without a per-stage repair budget. On a synthetic 5-bus network and on the IEEE 14-bus network at two repair-cost scales, the learned and baseline policies are compared on common evaluation paths. Without the budget, DFL is the cheapest policy on the 5-bus network; on the 14-bus network it does not outperform a near-sighted model-predictive control (MPC) baseline, but it beats repairing every failed component at the higher scale. Under a binding budget, DFL is the cheapest policy evaluated on both networks and at both scales, 14% to 23% below the next-best policy. On the 5-bus network, the mean cost of DFL is 1.7% (without the budget) and 1.8% (with it) above the exact optimum computed by dynamic programming. Within days of computation, sample average approximation yields costlier policies than DFL and the repair-everything heuristic, and stochastic dual dynamic integer programming remains far from convergence. DFL computes its decisions about as fast as the trivial heuristics and orders of magnitude faster than MPC. Since these conditions are not specific to power networks, the framework extends to other MSPs that share this structure.

papers.title: Homogenization with Shape-Evolving Microstructures: A Two-Phase Membrane Problem
papers.abstract: We study a diffusion problem in a highly heterogeneous periodic medium (characterized by a small scale parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll1$) where small inclusions are separated from the surrounding connected area by solute-impermeable membranes. These membranes are allowed to grow and deform under surface tension and osmotic pressure (driven by the concentration difference across the membrane). We prove existence of weak solutions on a time interval which is independent of the microscopic scale via a Schauder fixed-point argument by establishing spatial boundary Hölder estimates. For the homogenization limit $\varepsilon\to0$, we establish strong compactness of the outer concentration via time translates and then derive a stability estimate for the driven inner cell problems. The limit couples a macroscopic conservation law, with shape-dependent effective diffusion, to inner diffusion and membrane motion in each cell.

papers.title: Structure-preserving finite element method for the 2D MHD-$α$ turbulence system
papers.abstract: We propose a structure-preserving finite element method for the two-dimensional MHD-$α$ turbulence model, which filters the transport velocity at a length $α$ while retaining the ideal invariants of the original MHD equations, with the energy replaced by an $α$-dependent energy. The scheme preserves mass conservation and the magnetic Gauss law pointwise and satisfies discrete dissipation laws for the energy, the cross helicity and the mean square magnetic potential, which reduce to exact conservation in the ideal limit. The discrete systems are solved by an augmented Lagrangian preconditioner with monolithic geometric multigrid, observed to be robust with respect to the filter width $α$ and the Reynolds numbers, and to the mesh size for small time steps. The scheme converges at the optimal rates and agrees with a Fourier pseudo-spectral direct simulation of the original MHD equations at the large scales. In under-resolved flows, the unfiltered scheme has no numerical dissipation and accumulates energy at the grid scale. Filtering relieves this accumulation and a larger $α$ gives a more compact spectrum.
