Long-time simulations reproduce selective decay, including relaxation toward the Arnold-type bound and the inverse cascade of the mean square potential.

papers.title: Galois scalar extension of simple Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate the behaviour of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras under finite Galois field extensions. Given a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a finite Galois extension $\mathbb{K}/\mathbb{F}$ of degree $n = [\mathbb{K}:\mathbb{F}]$, we prove that if $L$ is isomorphic to a $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ viewed as an $\mathbb{F}$-algebra, then the scalar extension $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $n$ copies of $S$. Furthermore, for cyclic extensions of order a prime number, we show that if no such $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ exists, the extended algebra $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ remains simple. This framework provides a general mechanism to transfer structural and classification results across different ground fields. In addition, we examine the centroids of simple Lie algebras, proving that the dimension of the space of centroids is invariant under finite field extensions. As an application, we explicitly determine the structure of the spaces of centroids for simple Lie algebras over finite fields.

papers.title: Morse theory and a degree formula for the resonant singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We develop Morse theory for the singular Paneitz equation at resonant mass on closed four-manifolds with conical orders between minus one and zero and Paneitz kernel consisting of the constants. Under nondegeneracy of the reduced interactions and nonvanishing of the leading mass-defect coefficients, we classify the critical points at infinity by the sign of these coefficients. We compute their indices and their contributions to the relative homology of sublevels. The topology of very low sublevels is determined by weighted barycenters of strictly smaller total weight and by the negative Paneitz eigenspace. These results yield strong Morse inequalities and a Leray--Schauder degree formula at resonance, which also applies when genuine solutions are degenerate. On the round four-sphere with two conical points, the Morse inequalities give existence on an open set of data for which the degree vanishes.

papers.title: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems
papers.abstract: We consider whether the thermalization of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs (MFG) state, is constrained by a fundamental Planckian time scale, $\hbar/k_B T$. By requiring that the same process thermalizes a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, we obtain a lower bound on the thermalization time, irrespective of the specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the corresponding MFG states, and can therefore be computed from equilibrium properties alone. In its simplest form, it requires only a static susceptibility and an equilibrium variance of a system observable. We characterize this bound from weak to strong coupling in exactly solvable fermionic models, in the spin-boson model, and in a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. These models show that strong coupling can lift the Planckian constraint when the MFG state retains little information about the system Hamiltonian, while preserving it when that information is carried by system observables with substantial equilibrium fluctuations at frequencies below $k_B T/\hbar$. The bound is complementary to open-system speed limits, since it constrains the acquisition of information rather than the preparation of the target, and can remain informative at strong coupling even when the latter become trivial.

papers.title: Non-Intrusive Least-Squares Reduced Basis Methods: Black-Box Snapshots and Exact Residual Certificates
papers.abstract: For a parametrized linear first-order system, the least-squares functional at a conforming pair is the squared norm of the residual of the continuous problem, and it can be computed exactly. In this paper, we use this least-squares residual as the error certificate of reduced basis methods whose snapshots are computed by black-box solvers. The output of the solver is first made conforming by a reconstruction, and a flux is recovered by least-squares if the solver does not provide one. The online reduced problem minimizes the least-squares functional over the product of the space spanned by the snapshot fluxes and the space spanned by the snapshot potentials. It needs no inf--sup condition on the reduced spaces, and its certificate needs no stability constant. We discuss second-order elliptic equations, the Stokes equations, where only the velocity of a black-box solver is used, and linear transport equations with a moving inflow boundary. In the numerical experiments, the snapshots are computed by least-squares, conforming, nonconforming, stabilized, finite volume, and finite difference solvers. With adaptive meshes and the same tolerances, the greedy algorithm stops at the same or nearly the same reduced dimension for all solvers that accept a mesh.

papers.title: Stability of separable solutions to a fast diffusion system
papers.abstract: We study a Dirichlet fast diffusion system with symmetric linear cross-loss terms on a bounded smooth domain. A coupled Rayleigh quotient captures the variational structure of the coupling and is nonincreasing along sufficiently regular positive solution pairs. Under the common extinction and regularity hypotheses, this monotonicity and the energy identity yield upper and lower bounds \[ C^{-1}(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)} \le \|(u(t),v(t))\|_{L^{p+1}(Ω)} \le C(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)}. \] In the Sobolev subcritical range, a Lyapunov functional for the rescaled system yields a sequence of times $t_j\uparrow T^*$ along which the rescaled pair converges strongly in $H_0^1(Ω)\times H_0^1(Ω)$ to a nonnegative classical stationary solution pair. The integral lower bound excludes the trivial limiting pair, while the coupling with $α>0$ ensures that neither limiting component is identically zero. As a further property of the stationary system, we show that proportional components of a nontrivial nonnegative solution pair must coincide. We also construct a positive diagonal stationary solution pair by constrained minimization. Scalar upper comparison and a Bénilan--Crandall-type estimate for smooth positive diagonal solutions provide complementary links with the scalar fast diffusion equation.

papers.title: Ultrarank and ideal structure of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ideal structure of the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ for a coarse disjoint union $X = \bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} X_n$ of finite metric spaces, with a focus on ideals lying between the compact ideal $\mathcal{K}$ and the ghost ideal $\mathcal{G}$. To analyze these ideals, we introduce a nonstandard invariant called the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank of an operator, which is stable under compact perturbations and completely characterizes principal ideal inclusions in the block-diagonal Calkin algebra. Using the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank as an obstruction to ideal inclusion in $C^*_u(X)$, we construct an ideal between $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ that cannot be written as the intersection of any geometric ideal and the ghost ideal. On the positive side, when the averaging projection $P$ belongs to $C^*_u(X)$, we prove that the closed two-sided ideal $\langle P \rangle$ generated by $P$ equals $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if every ghost operator has finite ultrarank and $X$ has zero-density Property A, and we classify all closed two-sided ideals of $C^*_u(X)$ in this case.

papers.title: Optimal bounds for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-constant-power error-correcting cooling codes
papers.abstract: High temperatures have dramatic negative effects on interconnect performance. In a bus, whenever a wire changes its state from ``0'' to ``1'' or from ``1'' to ``0'', Joule heating causes the temperature to rise. Constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes, introduced in [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 66 (2020), 4804--4818], are coding schemes that can simultaneously control the peak temperature and the average power consumption of on-chip buses while providing error-correction capability for transmitted information. This paper establishes a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes for $t<w-3$ by some graph-theoretic techniques and the probabilistic method, and constructs several new families of optimal CPECC codes using the asymptotic existence result for GDDs. For $t\geq w-3$, this paper also provides a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes by some hypergraph-theoretic techniques, and several new families of CPECC codes attaining the resulting upper bounds using RBIBDs. The previous upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes in [arXiv:2608.08742] is a special case of our upper bound.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for chord integrals
papers.abstract: Chord integrals are moments of chord lengths and translation-invariant averages of dual quermassintegrals. In this paper, we prove their Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $q\in[1,n+2]\cup\{n+3\}$, with equality precisely for homothetic bodies. A transfer from symmetric dual quermassintegrals to covariogram level sets gives, in dimension two, the full range $1\leq q\leq5$. For every $0<q<1$, we establish the same inequality for simplices and an explicit factor version for all convex bodies. On the other hand, rectangular perturbations give counterexamples for every $q>n+1+β_*$, where $β_*\in(2,3)$. As consequences, we obtain Minkowski inequalities and uniqueness results for chord measures. We also prove Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for affine-section integrals and mixed Riesz energies.

papers.title: On Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners and their properties
papers.abstract: Bramble and Pasciak (Math. Comp., 1988) discovered a preconditioning method for linear algebraic systems in saddle point form, which under certain conditions transforms a symmetric indefinite saddle point matrix into a nonsymmetric matrix that is positive definite in some non-standard inner product. Thus, the method "removes" the indefiniteness of the problem, while retaining the property that the preconditioned system can be solved using an optimal Krylov subspace method with three-term recurrences. Since this well-known method has some limitations, several variants with potential improvements have been proposed in the literature. In this paper, we attempt a systematic assessment of the mathematical properties and practical efficiency of Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners. Our goal is to close some gaps in the understanding of these techniques. We identify and analyze the three main methods in this context, highlighting a variant that offers additional flexibility but has received little attention to date. We perform detailed spectral analyzes of the preconditioned matrices and illustrate our theoretical results on several numerical examples.

papers.title: The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation
papers.abstract: We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.

papers.title: Polynomial identities and primitivity in double extension regular algebras of type (14641)
papers.abstract: We determine which members of the twenty-six families of double extension regular algebras of type $(14641)$ in the Zhang--Zhang classification satisfy a polynomial identity. Retaining the scalar twist parameter, we compute the PI degree for twenty-one of the twenty-two families with PI members and give three possibilities for the remaining family. We establish exact primitivity criteria for the nondegenerate members of eight families and show that sixteen families have no primitive members. The proofs use monomial data, normal subalgebras and crossed products of quantum tori. Twisting by a root of unity preserves the PI property, whereas finite order of the double-extension determinant is necessary but not sufficient for an algebra in the list to be PI.

papers.title: On some problems regarding a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula
papers.abstract: In \cite{FT23}, we introduced the group-theoretical function $f(G) = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{H \le G} |\Aut(H)|$ for a finite group $G$ and posed three open problems concerning its values on noncyclic groups. In this note, we provide complete solutions to all three problems.

papers.title: Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
papers.abstract: We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs. As the diffusion strength increases, the waves end up moving in the same direction irrespective of the bistability. This direction is determined solely by the underlying structure of the heterogeneous tree. Our techniques also lead to sharper results for the homogeneous setting.

papers.title: Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe
papers.abstract: We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions and integrals. We prove that the associated period map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto a bounded, convex planar domain whose rational points parametrize the conformal equivalence classes of closed extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants. We conclude with a study of the global geometry of closed extremals.

papers.title: Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number
papers.abstract: We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element. By the criterion of Marche and Wolff, this proves Goldman's ergodicity conjecture for $g\ge 3$ and Euler numbers $e$ with $0<|e|\leq g-1$.

papers.title: List coloring degenerate graphs with requests
papers.abstract: We prove three results on the flexible list coloring of $d$-degenerate graphs. Following Dvořák, Norin and Postle [J. Graph Theory 2019], a graph $G$ is $(k,ε)$-flexible if for any assignment $L$ of lists of size $k$ to its vertices and any choice of requested colors by a set $\widehat V$ of the vertices from their respective lists, there is an $L$-coloring satisfying at least $ε|\widehat V|$ of the requests. The complete graph on $d+1$ vertices shows that if all $d$-degenerate graphs are $(k,ε)$-flexible for some list size $k$ and satisfaction ratio $ε$, then $k \geq d+1$ and $ε\leq\tfrac1{d+1}$. Our results concern values at or near these extremes. For list size $d+2$, we improve the satisfaction ratio from an inverse exponential to an inverse polynomial function of $d$. For satisfaction ratio $\tfrac1{d+1}$, we prove that it is achievable for list size $2d$ as well as $\left\lfloor(d+2)\left(2-\tfrac1e\right)\right\rfloor$ (which is less than $2d$ for $d\geq 9$).

papers.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
papers.abstract: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schrödinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

papers.title: Squeezing-preserving coherent control in Fourier-shaped optical lattices
papers.abstract: Motional squeezed states of atoms in optical lattices are affected by the anharmonicity of the trapping potential. Unequal vibrational energy spacings cause dephasing among the occupied motional-state coherences, leading to distortion of the wavepacket and a reduction in squeezing. We show numerically that adding a weak second or third spatial harmonic to a one-dimensional lattice slows the initial decay of the squeezing. Squeezed states are prepared by one or two sudden changes of the lattice depth. For each harmonic and each preparation scheme, we choose the harmonic amplitude that keeps the evolved state closest, on average over 1 ms, to its evolution in a harmonic trap. We then compare the squeezing with that in a sinusoidal lattice with the same initial squeezing and trap frequency. In all four cases studied, the successive squeezing maxima initially decay more slowly in the shaped lattice. The improvement arises because the optimal harmonic nearly equalizes the two dominant vibrational level spacings over the region occupied by the squeezed wave packet, which canceling the quartic term of the potential alone does not achieve. Because the amplitude of the added harmonic is static and can be produced with existing Fourier-synthesis techniques, lattice shaping offers a simple way to preserve motional squeezing without additional time-dependent control.

papers.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
papers.abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $ρ_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $ρ_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).

papers.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on vector bundles II: the non-simple case
papers.abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system on the space of Fubini-Study metrics on a polarized compact Kähler manifold. Sano proved that if there exists a balanced metric for the polarization, then this dynamical system always converges to the balanced metric provided that the automorphism group is discrete (\cite{S}). In \cite{DKLR}, Douglas, et.\ al., conjecture that the same holds in the case of vector bundles. In \cite{Se}, we proved their conjecture under the assumption that the bundle is simple. In this note, we remove the simplicity assumption. The main tool is Thompson's metric on the space of Hermitian inner products on the space of holomorphic sections, with respect to which the generalized $T$-operator is non-expanding.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Single-Control Null Controllability of Stochastic Heat Equations
papers.abstract: We disprove the conjecture that a single localized drift control suffices for null controllability of stochastic parabolic equations with bounded adapted coefficients. On a bounded interval with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we construct a deterministic, nonnegative smooth noise coefficient supported at positive distance from the control interval. One fixed nonzero smooth initial state cannot be driven to zero almost surely at any positive time by any progressively measurable control with finite expected $L^2$ energy. The proof uses products of Brownian increments in the adjoint terminal data to keep the initial pairing bounded away from zero while the observation norm tends to zero. On the flat torus, the construction yields counterexamples in every Gevrey class of order $s>1$ whenever the complement of the control set contains an open ball. Thus Gevrey regularity above order one cannot replace analyticity as a general sufficient condition for null controllability.

papers.title: Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree
papers.abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support of $N=n+k+1$ monomials, and we study the topological degree of $F$ on the positive orthant. In a previous paper we computed this topological degree in terms of signs of maximal minors, under a half-space condition which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. Here we use these formulas, together with their translation on the Gale dual side, to bound the topological degree. Our main result is a Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree, which is as simple as the classical one: for two variables, the absolute value of the topological degree is at most half the number of cyclic sign changes, at the vertices of the Newton polygon, of the coefficients of any linear combination of the two equations, and similar statements hold in any dimension and on the Gale dual side. Our second result is a fewnomial bound: for generic exponents and coefficients, we get $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the maximal number of facets of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $N$ vertices, and this bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Our third result is a symmetry: using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible values of the topological degree is the same for the parameters $(n,k)$ and $(k,n)$.

papers.title: Localizing spectra and pseudospectra of a class of unbounded operators on Hilbert space
papers.abstract: We use a localization technique to bound and approximate the spectrum and the pseudospectra of a certain class of possibly non-normal, generally unbounded but closed operators on $L^2(X)$, where $X$ is either a) a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group $G$, not necessarily Abelian, with identity, a proper metric, and a left Haar measure or it is b) a uniformly discrete subset of $G$ with the counting measure. We treat the discrete and continuous cases b) and a) simultaneously. Our results yield computable subsets and supersets of the pseudospectra of $H$ that converge to the corresponding pseudospectrum in Attouch-Wets distance as the size parameter $L$ in our localization procedure goes to infinity. We illustrate our findings with unbounded band operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and with Schrödinger operators with $L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ potentials acting on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

papers.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
papers.abstract: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.

papers.title: CLT for Linear Spectral Statistics of sample covariances of superimposition of Separable Covariance Components
papers.abstract: Suppose $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ are $p\times n$ random matrices with entries having zero mean and unit variance and $p/n \to c \in (0,\infty)$. We construct the sample covariance matrix $S_n = \frac{1}{n}XX^*$ where $X =\sum_{r=1}^K X_r$, where $X_r = A_r^\frac{1}{2}Z_rB_r^\frac{1}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $A_r,B_r$ are sequences of positive semi-definite matrices of dimensions $p\times p$ and $n\times n$, respectively that are are simultaneously digaonalizable within themselves. As an extension of our previous work related to the L.S.D. of such classes of matrices, we show that the linear spectral statistics arising from the spectra of $S_n$ have Gaussian limits under assumptions of fourth moment bounds on the entries of $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and convergence of the joint spectral distribution of $\{A_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and $\{B_r\}_{r=1}^K$ to probability distributions over $\mathbb{R}_+^K$ with compact support.

papers.title: On the performance of nanoscale detection methods in NV-center spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) in subfemtoliter volumes operates in a regime where statistical fluctuations of the nuclear magnetization can exceed its thermal mean. Solid-state quantum sensors such as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are sensitive enough to detect NMR signals from such small volumes, which has motivated several detection protocols, based either on correlating the statistical polarization or on coherently detecting hyperpolarized samples. Here we bring Qdyne, CS, MCS, and CASR into a single framework for nanoscale samples. Specifically, we derive a unified analytical expression for the SNR and spin-number sensitivity applicable to all four protocols under consistent experimental conditions. Numerical simulations of the full measurement sequences confirm this expression over the whole range of parameters explored. This formulation enables a quantitative comparison of their performance while accounting for the distinct measurement sequences, acquisition times, and other related parameters. Using the SNR and the spin-number sensitivity as figures of merit, we identify which protocol performs best in each experimental regime, thereby providing a practical guide for choosing and tuning the most suitable method for a given experiment.

papers.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
papers.abstract: For a finite dimensional semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the multiplicity $c_{λμ}^ν$ of an irreducible $V(ν),$ inside the tensor product $V(λ)\otimes V(μ),$ of two highest weight irreducible representations can be realised as the dimension of the Kostant--Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan multiplicity space inside $V(λ)$, $V(μ)$ or $V(ν)$. A result of Panyushev and Yakimova shows how to split the multiplicity space for $c_{λλ}^ν$ inside $V(ν)$ into symmetric and alternating parts when $V(λ)$ is self-dual. For finite-dimensional semisimple or symmetric Kac--Moody, we extend this to Kostant--Kumar modules $K(λ,w,λ)=\mathfrak{Ug}(v_λ\otimes v_{wλ})$ when $w=w^{-1},$ and for all dominant weights $λ.$ We show that the multiplicities of an irreducible in the symmetric and alternating parts of $K(λ,w,λ)$ are given by the dimensions of the eigenspaces of the Tits lift $\widetilde w$ of $w$ on the multiplicity space corresponding to eigenvalues $\pm 1$. This recovers the result for the full tensor product by letting $w=w_0,$ the longest element of the Weyl group. In type A, we also discuss connections to a combinatorial interpretation due to Carré and Leclerc in terms of domino tableaux.

papers.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
papers.abstract: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, μ)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, μ)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, μ)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, μ)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, μ)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.

papers.title: Pettis integrability of $L^1$-functions in locally convex spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, for a Hausdorff locally convex space $E$, we investigate conditions under which every Lusin-measurable $L^1$-function $γ:[0,1]\to E$ is Pettis integrable. We show that this property on $E$ is local and equivalent to $E$ being absolutely summable and satisfying the metric convex compactness property. Via examples, we show that these two properties are independent. Moreover, we establish sufficient conditions, for a Lusin-measurable weakly integrable function with values in the topological dual $E'$, to be Gelfand integrable.

papers.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincaré duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordström, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and Lê, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in Lê's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

papers.title: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective
papers.abstract: Variational principles have played a fundamental role in the development of modern mathematics, physics, and scientific computing. From the principles of least action in mechanics to the calculus of variations and the variational formulation of partial differential equations, they have provided a powerful framework for understanding complex problems and designing reliable numerical methods. In recent years, Machine Learning has introduced a new computational paradigm, in which highly expressive nonlinear function spaces and large-scale minimisation problems play a central role. In these notes, we explore the connection between these two frameworks. We develop a variational and numerical-analysis perspective on Machine Learning algorithms, focusing in particular on their formulation as nonlinear minimisation problems. We investigate how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness acquire new interpretations in this setting, and how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can govern the behaviour of neural-network approximations. This perspective provides a mathematical framework for understanding existing ML algorithms while also suggesting new approaches to their design. In particular, alternative and strongly coercive variational principles can lead to more stable, reliable, and potentially more efficient computational methods.

papers.title: Cross-chip transfer in quantum photonic neural networks
papers.abstract: Fabrication variability makes it difficult to reuse one set of trained parameters across a batch of quantum photonic chips without additional chip-specific optimization. We examine how device-specific compensation and task tolerance shape cross-chip performance. For squared operator loss, local analysis predicts that reducing own-chip error through compensation incurs an increase in expected loss on independent chips. We use Monte Carlo ensemble training (MC-ENS), informed by an available statistical model of fabrication-induced parameter errors. It optimizes one shared parameter set for each task or target at a given fabrication scale by averaging losses over simulated chip realizations resampled from this model. Numerical simulations of a quantum photonic neural network compare MC-ENS with single-chip training, sharpness-aware training and a covariance-informed variant. For CNOT synthesis and Ising dynamics, MC-ENS reduces mean conditional process infidelity and increases mean postselection probability on unseen chips. In classification, high accuracy can persist despite substantial changes in the optical transformation. The decision-margin analysis shows when fabrication-induced score shifts are likely to change predicted labels. The trained shared parameters can be reused without device-specific retraining on unseen chips drawn from the same fabrication distribution.

papers.title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
papers.abstract: The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.

papers.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
papers.abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $Γ$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $Γ$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $Γ$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

papers.title: The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs
papers.abstract: A $Γ$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $Γ$. Fix a finite abelian group $Γ$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist. The result previously appeared only in the author's 2009 PhD thesis. This proof uses a reduction to unbreakable graphs and recent structure theorems for graphs drawn on a surface, and was found with the help of AI.

papers.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
papers.abstract: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(θ)=|q_n(e^{iθ})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-Γ(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.

papers.title: Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results
papers.abstract: This paper investigates inverse problems for backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), with a particular focus on the converse comparison theorem and the uniqueness of generators solely through the initial values of the corresponding solutions. To this end, we develop a forward-SDE representation approach that combines a contradiction argument with a representation of generators in terms of solutions to associated forward stochastic differential equations (SDEs). As one of the main consequences, we prove that an ordering between two $g$-expectations necessarily implies the pointwise comparability of their generators, without requiring any additional structural assumptions beyond the standard Lipschitz condition. This removes the continuity, $y$-independence, and deterministic assumptions required in previous works, thereby yielding a complete solution to the converse comparison problem for $g$-expectations under the standard Lipschitz framework and, at the same time, establishing a general uniqueness theorem for generators of BSDEs.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ρ,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ρ(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ρ$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: Cooperative colorings of cycles and uniform cycle factors
papers.abstract: A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring. Together with known bounds, this determines, for every $\ell\geq3$, the least number $m$ such that every $m$ graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, have a cooperative coloring. For $\ell\geq3$, this number is four when $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ and three otherwise. These results answer two questions of Aharoni, Holzman, Howard, and Sprüssel.

papers.title: The hitting time index: bounds, a sharp threshold, the proof of a conjecture and the disproof of another conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove some new upper and lower bounds for the hitting time index ($HT$ index) of an $n$-vertex graph, showing along the way that the largest order of the index is $n^5$ and the smallest is $n^3$. More specifically, we prove the conjecture that the smallest value of the index is $\frac{n(n-1)^2}{2}$, which is attained by the complete graph. We also find a sharp threshold for the minimal degree $δ$ so that the $HT$ index goes from an $n^4$ order to an $n^3$ order if the threshold is surpassed. We disprove the conjecture that the largest value of the index is attained by the $n$-path, and look at the lollipop graphs, some of which attain the $n^5$ order, and seem to be the natural candidates among which the largest value of the index should be attained.

papers.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

papers.title: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that involve parameterised quantum circuits and classical optimisation. VQAs have found applications in simulation, optimisation, and machine learning. However, their scalability is hindered by flat landscapes-regions in the parameter space where gradients vanish exponentially small. In such regimes, gradient-based optimisation methods fail because parameter updates become ineffective in the absence of informative gradients. In this work, we propose a search-based restart framework to escape flat regions in structured flat landscapes, in which small trainable regions exist within a large flat landscape. This framework approaches the plateau escape as a search problem and locates trainable regions. The optimiser's parameters stop updating when the gradients vanish, and the method then searches over-sampled points to identify landscapes with nonzero gradients. We provide theoretical estimates of the number of jumps and the probability of escape from flat landscapes. This restarts the local optimisation process and avoids stagnation. We tested this framework on synthetic functions that mimic structured flat landscapes and a real quantum circuit cost landscape. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that Search-for-Gradient improves optimisation performance in structured flat landscapes. The proposed framework assumes the existence of a trainable region with nonzero measure and will not work if it has zero measure. Our framework can be integrated with existing VQAs to improve trainability and robustness.

papers.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
papers.abstract: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

papers.title: Extremals and Normalized Solutions for a Critical Weighted Choquard Equation
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the weighted Choquard equation \[ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=λ|x|^{-2a}u+β|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp} \left( \int_{\mathbb R^N} \frac{|u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^μ|y|^{bp}}\,dy \right) |u|^{p-2}u &&\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx&=ρ^2, \end{aligned} \right. \] where $N\ge3$, $a<(N-2)/2$, $a<b<a+1$, $2<q<2^\sharp$, $0<μ<N$, $p=(2N-μ)/(N-2d)$ is the upper Stein--Weiss critical exponent, $d=1-b+a$, $2^\sharp=2N/(N-2-2a+2b)$, $ρ>0$ is prescribed, $β>0$, and $λ\in\mathbb R$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. Assuming $p>2$, we establish existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions in different mass regimes, including negative-energy ground states for small $β$ and positive-energy second solutions under suitable assumptions, as well as ground states in the mass-critical and mass-supercritical cases under explicit conditions

papers.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

papers.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
papers.abstract: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional Zhidkov space
papers.abstract: We show global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the Zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. For the usual nonlinear Schrödinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. Here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. Global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+H^1$ follows. We also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to different nonlinearities.

papers.title: Degree-respecting labellings with ordered neighbour sums
papers.abstract: In an exhaustive enumeration of hydrocarbons with only single bonds, carbon skeletons are generated as adjacency matrices and pruned by two rules: a vertex of larger degree receives a smaller label, and among vertices of equal degree, a vertex whose adjacency row is the larger binary integer receives a smaller label. The pruning is sound only if every skeleton admits a labelling obeying both rules. We prove that such a labelling exists for every finite simple graph, connected or not and with no bound on the degrees, and that the same holds when the weights $2^i$ of the labels $i$ are replaced by any strictly increasing real weights. The proof takes, among the labellings that order vertices by non-increasing degree, one minimising the sum over edges of the products of the endpoint weights.

papers.title: Mean field game value multifunction: dynamic programming principle
papers.abstract: We study mean field games (MFGs) on the torus with non-degenerate diffusion, in a regime (no monotonicity) where multiple solutions exist for the same data. In this setting the value of a representative player is not a function of the initial time and distribution, and the classical master equation loses its meaning. We describe the dependence of the value on the initial data by a multivalued mapping, the value multifunction, assigning to each initial time and distribution the set of value functions of all solutions of the MFG starting from that data. Our main result gives a sufficient condition for a closed multifunction to be a value multifunction, namely, it must satisfy a dynamic programming principle formulated on proper time subintervals, expressed as invariance of its graph under the forward operators generated by equilibria of the game. This replaces the global requirement that each value be produced by a solution of the forward-backward system on the whole time interval by a local, time-consistent condition together with closedness, which carries the terminal condition. The result is the second-order analogue of the viability approach previously developed for first-order mean field games. We reformulate solutions of the mean field game in terms of relaxed equilibria, show that the closure of a value multifunction is again a value multifunction, and prove that the forward operators compose as a semigroup. We also present an explicit example in which a single terminal cost produces at least two solutions for every initial time in an interval, while solutions are unique for initial times sufficiently close to the horizon.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for the early fault-tolerant quantum computing (early-FTQC) era that estimates minute energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces, at a lower sampling cost than existing phase-estimation methods. Such energy derivatives, accessed as the small energy difference induced by an infinitesimal parameter shift, are central to quantum simulation in chemistry and materials science. Although Statistical Phase Estimation (SPE) is well-suited to energy estimation in this era, applying it to an energy difference demands a sampling complexity that scales with the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian, which grows with system size. Our algorithm overcomes this by incorporating two time-evolution operators, corresponding to the Hamiltonians before and after the parameter shift, into a single quantum circuit, which is combined with a non-adaptive, statistically sampled reconstruction in the energy-difference domain. This reduces the relevant scale from the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian to that of the operator norm of the Hamiltonian derivative and the parameter shift, thereby lowering the sampling complexity. We further propose the joint estimation of energy eigenvalues and their differences, giving a holistic view of the energy landscape. Numerical simulations and resource estimations on prototypical systems, such as the Fermi-Hubbard model, demonstrate the resulting reductions in required resources without compromising precision. This positions energy-difference estimation as a practical task for early-FTQC devices, opening a route to molecular forces, response properties, and excited-state energy differences.

papers.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
papers.abstract: A latent index $J\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ is drawn from a prior $π$. Conditional on $J=j$, a gambler observes random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ drawn independently from a non-negative component distribution $F_j$. The gambler knows $n$, the prior $π$, and the component distributions $F_1,\ldots,F_k$, but not $J$, observes the values sequentially, and selects at most one value at the time it is revealed. We show that the largest $α$ such that the gambler can guarantee to select a value of $α\cdot\mathbb{E}[\max_iX_i]$ in expectation, for all distributions where this expectation is finite, is \[ α=\frac1e+\frac{1}{k^{2/3+o(1)}}. \] The lower bound is achieved by the better of two variants of the standard secretary rule. The upper bound uses a finely tuned instance of the common-scale model, which scales a sequence of independent random variables by a single latent variable.

papers.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
papers.abstract: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. A GPU-based finite-difference implementation, released as an open-source Python library, achieves speedups greater than x30 for realistic mesh sizes, making three-dimensional simulations on realistic geometries computationally tractable. This provides a basis for future in-silico studies of treatment strategies, such as testing antiviral or immunomodulatory therapies, and for patient-specific simulations based on individual liver geometries, paving the way towards personalized healthcare.

papers.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
papers.abstract: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

papers.title: A square analogue of the diamond order and a unified approach to the plus order
papers.abstract: We introduce the square order $\le^\square$ on group invertible matrices, defined by $A^3=ABA$ and $A\le^s B$, where $\le^s$ is the space pre-order. It is the group inverse analogue of the diamond order: $A\le^\square B$ if and only if $A^\#\le^- B^\#$. Using its block representation, we characterize the reverse order law $(AB)^\#=B^\#A^\#$ for $A\le^\square B$. In contrast to the Moore--Penrose case, the conditions $A\le^- B$ and $(B-A)^\#=B^\#-A^\#$ do not characterize the sharp order; instead, they lead to new partial orders between the sharp and square orders. We also develop a framework where the plus order replaces the minus order in Mitra's unified theory. For a map $\mathcal G$ assigning to each matrix $A$ a subset of its inner inverses, we define $A\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A=PBQ$ for some pair $(P,Q)=(AA^-,A^-A)$, $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$, whereas Mitra's relation requires $A=PB=BQ$, and $A\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A^-\le^-B^-$ for some reflexive $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$ and $B^-\in\mathcal G(B)$. When $\mathcal G(A)$ consists of a single reflexive inverse, we characterize the transitivity of $\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}$ in terms of $\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}$, and in general we give a sufficient condition for both to be partial orders. For maps defined by the equations of the Moore--Penrose, group, core and dual core inverses, both relations coincide and only nine arise: the plus, diamond and square orders, two new orders based on core inverses, and four further relations. In Mitra's theory, they yield exactly the minus, star, sharp, core and dual core orders and the one-sided star and sharp orders.

papers.title: Deterministic integer factorization from abundance decisions
papers.abstract: We prove that deciding whether a positive integer is abundant is equivalent to complete integer factorization under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. In particular, abundance can be decided in deterministic polynomial time if and only if integers can be factored in deterministic polynomial time. Our reduction uses carefully chosen coprime multipliers to recover exact divisor sums from abundance queries, and then extracts the complete prime factorization of an integer $n$ deterministically from the divisor sums of $O(\log n)$ consecutive powers of $n$. Altogether, factoring $n$ requires $O((\log n)^4)$ adaptive abundance queries, each at an integer of $O((\log n)^6)$ binary digits.

papers.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
papers.abstract: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

papers.title: Ancilla-Assisted Accelerated Readout of Transmon Qubits
papers.abstract: We present a scheme for accelerating dispersive readout of superconducting transmon qubits. Dispersive readout works by weakly coupling the target transmon to a resonator, such that the resonator experiences a state-dependent frequency shift, which can then be read out. Our scheme introduces an ancillary transmon coupled to the same resonator. By appropriately correlating its state with that of the target transmon (using a fast CNOT gate), we show that the resonator frequency shift is approximately doubled, halving the required measurement duration to maintain the same quality. We present analytical results within the dispersive approximation, before employing and extending the recently introduced technique of branch analysis to account for ionization and other nonlinearities. Using this, and taking into account realistic noise and gate times, we show that our scheme allows measurement durations smaller by a factor of approximately 0.6, demonstrating that it offers a viable route for accelerating measurements of transmon qubits.

papers.title: Polynomial-degree-robust saturation on triangular meshes
papers.abstract: We prove a polynomial-degree-robust ($p$-robust) saturation property for conforming finite element approximations of the Poisson equation on shape-regular triangular meshes. Previously, a $p$-robust saturation estimate for the spectral method on a square was proved in [C. Canuto et al., A saturation property for the spectral-Galerkin approximation of a Dirichlet problem in a square, ESAIM Math. Model. Numer. Anal., 53 (2019), pp. 987--1003]. For every fixed $λ>1$, increasing the polynomial degree from $p$ to any $q\geq\lceilλp\rceil+3$ reduces the energy error by a factor $α_λ\in(0,1)$ independent of $p$ and the mesh size, up to a data oscillation term.

papers.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.

papers.title: Weak-strong stability and uniqueness of measure-valued solutions to (nonlocal) pressureless Euler-type systems
papers.abstract: We consider the pressureless Euler equation possibly coupled with non-local forces like the Poisson and alignment interactions. We overcome the lack of strict convexity in the relative entropy inequality that arises from the lack of pressure. The key to this result is the appropriate framework of the solution scheme utilizing the generalized Young measure which yields extra structural properties for the oscillation and concentration parts of the measure-valued solution. We overcome the problem of density mismatch via two complementary techniques. The first takes advantage of a Figalli--Kang-type transport inequality. The second involves establishing a generation lemma for the generalized Young measure which simultaneously establishes $L^2$-based control in flat metric between the measure-valued density and the density generating sequence.

papers.title: A Characterization of Douglas Weights
papers.abstract: A weight $ω$ on the unit disc is a \emph{Douglas weight} if the $ω$-energy of the Poisson extension of every Lipschitz function $f$ on the unit circle equals $\iint|f(ζ)-f(λ)|^2\,d\J_ω$ for some positive symmetric measure $\J_ω$ off the diagonal. For radial weights, we show that this holds if and only if \[ j_ω(θ) = \int_0^1 \frac{ω(r)}{r}\, \partial_θ^2 P(r^2,θ)\,dr \geq 0, \qquad 0<θ\leqπ, \] where $P(x,θ)$ denotes the Poisson kernel. We also obtain a complete characterization of the Douglas weights among arbitrary weights. The class of Douglas weights strictly contains the nonnegative superharmonic weights, and we give examples that are neither superharmonic nor subharmonic.

papers.title: Geometry, masking and selection in Differential Evolution and SOMA on quantum state manifolds
papers.abstract: Differential Evolution (DE) and the Self-Organizing Migrating Algorithm (SOMA) generate new candidates through vector arithmetic: they subtract population members, scale the difference, and mask coordinates. Many practical search spaces are not vector spaces, however. Rotation angles are periodic, normalized states lie on spheres and projective spaces, and circuit parameters are coupled through the quantum states they produce. We present a systematic study of how such geometry affects the core operations of DE and SOMA. Keeping the operators and selection rules fixed, we replace only their geometric primitives and separate the effects of difference construction, masking, and selection in a large paired numerical study covering textbook manifolds and variational quantum problems. Geometry-consistent differences make full-crossover (CR = 1) DE significantly better on 16 of 31 non-Euclidean configurations, with no significant deterioration, and the advantage persists when the measured computational cost of each variant is taken into account. The effect is largest where ordinary subtraction misrepresents distances between candidates: success on periodic synchronization rises from 44% to 100%, and on a positive-definite matrix problem from 1% to 99%. On six- qubit variational eigensolvers, shortest-path angular differences reduce the mean final loss by 90% for about 3% extra runtime. The improvements come with two contrasting diversity patterns, more effective population contraction or preserved population diversity, so higher acceptance rates do not necessarily indicate better search. Crossover masks interact with geometry: they can favor cheaper retractions and can increase the distance moved in quantum-state space when circuit parameters are coupled. These results give practical rules for designing population-based optimizers on non-Euclidean and quantum search spaces.

papers.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
papers.abstract: For a polynomial map $φ\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $φ^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $dφ$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $φ$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set. These results apply to every counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture and to families of Keller maps. For the explicit three-dimensional counterexample we show that $\A^3$ is the variety of binary cubic forms of a special shape with a marked simple root, and that $F$ forgets the root. This gives the degree, the fibres, the non-properness set, the monodromy and the structure of the twisted ternary algebra. Three examples modelled on weighted scrolls illustrate equivariance, degeneration to an automorphism, and an $A_1$ singularity of the fibre.

papers.title: The capillary $L_{p}$ dual Christoffel-Minkowski-type problem for $p\geq q$ with $1\leq k\leq n$
papers.abstract:
We study the following fully nonlinear $k$-Hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_θ$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<θ<π/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) &=fh^{p-1} igl(h^2+|
abla h|^2 igr)^{ rac{k+1-q}{2}} &&	ext{in }\mathcal{C}_θ,\ 
abla_μh&=\cotθ\,h &&	ext{on }\partial\mathcal{C}_θ. \end{aligned} ight. $$ Under suitable convexity and boundary assumptions on $f$, we establish the existence of positive smooth strictly convex solutions for $p\geq q$, together with uniqueness when $p>q$ and $p\geq 1$. In the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $C^0$ estimates without normalization. We overcome this difficulty using a logarithmic gradient estimate and a normalized approximation with uniqueness up to dilation.

papers.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
papers.abstract: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.

papers.title: Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number
papers.abstract: We use number-theoretic tools to find an explicit and effective obstruction for a knot to have algebraic unknotting number equal to $1$. As an example, we show that the connected sum of $T(2,5)$ (the cinquefoil) and $-T(2,3)$ (the negative trefoil) has algebraic unknotting number $1$, even though $T(2,5)$ has algebraic unknotting number $2$.

papers.title: The confined discrete DLSS equation: gradient flow structure and long-time asymptotics
papers.abstract: We propose and analyse a structure-preserving discretization of the fourth-order DLSS equation in dynamically rescaled variables leading to a linear confinement on the one-dimensional real line. The scheme is obtained as a discrete analogue of the Carrillo--Toscani splitting. It allows for a new interpretation of the DLSS equation as gradient flow of the relative entropy with respect to a combined diffusive and transport metric, extending the structure of the discretization introduced in our earlier work with Giuseppe Savaré for the unconfined equation. We prove global existence of positive solutions and, as the main analytical result, exponential decay of the relative entropy towards the discrete Gaussian equilibrium. The decay rate is obtained via a discrete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The resulting rate is consistent with the continuum rate and converges to it from below in the vanishing mesh-size limit. Numerical results illustrate and confirm our findings.

papers.title: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
papers.abstract: Quantum reflection is a counter-intuitive process occurring when an atom is reflected by a rapidly-varying attraction towards a surface, for example the Casimir-Polder force. The reflection probability depends on the attractive potential and on the mass of the atom. For hydrogen isotopes, the potentials are nearly identical whereas significant differences in quantum reflection come from the effect of atomic mass. We calculate the quantum reflection probability for the three isotopes H, D or T falling onto the plane surface of an intrinsic silicon bulk. We show that the results obey scaling laws determined by scattering lengths calculated from theory. Moreover the scattering lengths also obey scaling laws with respect to atomic masses of the isotopes.

papers.title: Generic non-convergence of low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics on $\mathbb Z^2$
papers.abstract: We study how typical convergence is, in the topological sense of Baire category, for the heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the nearest-neighbour, zero-field Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ started from translation-invariant initial laws. At sufficiently low positive temperature, we show that the initial laws whose evolution has both the plus and the minus phase as weak subsequential limits form a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of translation-invariant laws with the weak topology. Consequently, the initial laws for which the dynamics converges in distribution form a meagre set, which gives a partial answer to an open problem posed by Liggett. In particular, a large initial magnetisation does not force convergence to the plus phase, even for spatially ergodic initial laws. The proof combines equilibrium and mixing estimates of Gheissari and Sly with a periodic grid of plus spins of vanishing density and Baire's theorem, and it applies to all reversible monotone Glauber dynamics for the Ising model.

papers.title: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property
papers.abstract: We characterize the time-consistency of convex, cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures in terms of their minimal penalty. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities, which factorize across an intermediate date in many ways, according to how the discount is allocated to the two periods. We introduce an infimal cocycle property, in which the penalty is the infimum over all such factorizations, and show that it is equivalent to time-consistency, with the infimum attained. This holds on $L^\infty$ under continuity from below, and on $L^p$, $p<\infty$, without continuity assumptions. In the cash-additive case it reduces to the classical cocycle property. For risk measures induced by BSDEs, it represents the dynamic programming principle of a stochastic control problem whose value is the penalty.

papers.title: Veronese Classification of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics
papers.abstract: We prove that every linearly full, irreducible conformal minimal immersion of constant Gaussian curvature and finite isotropy order from the two-sphere into a complex hyperquadric comes from a member of a Veronese sequence. The result holds at every finite isotropy order, without an unramifiedness or additional Frenet-norm polynomiality assumption. Both the associated projective harmonic sequence and the target harmonic sequence are totally unramified as consequences. If the replacement depth is \(\ell\) and the holomorphic seed spans \(\mathbb{CP}^m\), the curvature is \(K=2/((2\ell+1)m-2\ell^2)\) in the Grassmannian normalization. Real Gram data characterize the admissible embeddings and give an algebraic converse. The proof uses holomorphic Pfaffian norm identities, degree estimates that retain all ramification divisors, and a valuation argument that identifies the retained lines with seed Frenet lines.

papers.title: Simultaneous Inversion of Drift and Potential in the Fractional Magnetic Schrödinger Equation
papers.abstract: We study the Calderón problem for the fractional magnetic Schrödinger equation with drift in the bivariate additive framework. When the magnetic potential $A$ is known and fixed, we prove that the drift $b$ and the scalar potential $q$ can be simultaneously and uniquely determined from exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements. When $A$ is unknown, we prove that the triple $(A,b,q)$ can only be recovered up to a natural gauge equivalence class, and that the drift $b$ is a gauge invariant, hence uniquely determined. The proofs rely on the Alessandrini identity, Runge approximation, and the unique continuation property for fractional magnetic operators. Furthermore, we have developed a numerical reconstruction framework that combines finite difference discretization, radial basis function surrogate modeling, and smoothed TV regularization. One-dimensional and two-dimensional numerical examples have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and supported the theoretical uniqueness result.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
papers.abstract: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,μ)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,μ)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes.
