For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

papers.title: A General Framework for Identifying the Joint Potential Outcome Distribution through Support Restrictions
papers.abstract: Many causal estimands depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes, which is generally not identifiable because only one potential outcome can be observed for each unit. To obtain identification, researchers often impose assumptions such as monotonicity and exclusion restriction that constrain the support of this joint distribution. For treatments and outcomes that each take finitely many values, we define a similarity matrix whose entries count, for each pair of potential outcome strata, the number of treatments yielding the same outcome. We then prove that, under unconfoundedness, identification holds if and only if this matrix is invertible, yielding a criterion directly verifiable from the support. In addition, we derive an identification formula for the joint distribution under these support restrictions and show that an average causal estimand is identifiable if and only if its integrand admits an additive representation on the restricted support. Finally, we derive sharp testable implications of the support restriction. Our results unify and generalize a broad range of identification results in the literature.

papers.title: The Descriptive Complexity of Continuous Selections with Prescribed Hausdorff dimension of the Graph
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of continuous selections of set-valued functions with prescribed Hausdorff dimension of their graphs. We consider Hausdorff-continuous functions defined on the unit interval whose values are nonempty compact subsets of the real line. We prove that, for every $β\in[1,2]$, the collection of all such functions admitting a continuous selection whose graph has Hausdorff dimension $β$ is $Σ^1_1$-complete and hence is not Borel. Further, we show that this result holds even when the set-valued functions have totally disconnected values. Thus, we obtain a complete classification of the descriptive complexity of the existence problem for all possible Hausdorff dimensions of continuous graphs over the unit interval.

papers.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
papers.abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

papers.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
papers.abstract: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.

papers.title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

papers.title: Mixed moment of twisted modular $L$-functions and Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a Hecke holomorphic cusp form for $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $q=p^γ$ be a prime power, where $p$ is an arbitrary prime and $γ\geq 2$. We establish an asymptotic formula for the mixed moment of $L(s,f\otimesχ)$ and $L(s,χ)$ on the central point. We also establish an upper bound for the smoothed sum of Hecke eigenvalues twisted by hyper-Kloosterman sums modulo powers of $2$.

papers.title: Weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to Nakao's problem in three dimensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the Duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. The estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. As an application, we study Nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. Under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces. The result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. The proof combines the new Duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.

papers.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
papers.abstract: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials. (ii) We determine the signs of the nonzero Schur coefficients of modular Schur functions, show that their absolute values are at most the factorial of the block weight, and characterize equality. (iii) Over an infinite field of prime characteristic, a modular Schur polynomial is a simple polynomial character exactly when its indexing partition satisfies the Carter condition, provided the number of variables is at least the degree. Thus we prove three conjectures formulated by Walker (1994). We also use the Heisenberg operators from the Schur coefficient calculation to prove positivity for Macdonald characters. After centering the Macdonald parameters at one and negating the auxiliary variables, the normalized power-sum matrix entries of the Macdonald creation operator have nonnegative integer coefficients, which yields nonnegative rational coefficients for normalized Macdonald characters. The result for the creation operator confirms a conjecture of Ben Dali and D'Adderio (2024).

papers.title: Normal and Unitary Operators on Smooth Banach Spaces via the Duality Mapping
papers.abstract: This article extends the classical notions of normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces through the duality mapping. The class of normal operators introduced in this setting contains, as a special case, the self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces defined via the duality mapping. We establish several characterisations of these operators and investigate their fundamental properties. In particular, we examine various spectral properties of normal operators on smooth Banach spaces. These results demonstrate that many fundamental aspects of the classical theory of normal and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces persist in the smooth Banach space setting.

papers.title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We describe an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the syntax and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), which are natural quantum circuit analogs of classical tensor networks. An HQC uses mid-circuit measurements and resets on a small subset of "physical" qubits whose measurement outcomes become correlated through coupling with a register of persistent "ancilla" qubits, analogous to the physical and bond indices of a tensor network. Hence, an HQC with fixed qubit resources can efficiently generate samples from a large quantum state, and adding qubits to the HQC ansatz has the effect of exponentially increasing the effective bond dimension. Our machine learning approach provides mechanisms for harnessing both features of HQCs by extrapolating the syntax (e.g., a sequence of gates, measurements, and resets) and parameters (e.g., the angles appearing in single-qubit rotations) from a dataset of HQCs to longer or more expressive HQCs. We demonstrate the methodology and its performance on an analytically solvable dataset formed by a vector-valued generalization of the W-state. Finally, we provide an outlook for usage of the methodology for scaling the effective bond dimensions of HQCs in quantum simulation.

papers.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
papers.abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

papers.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
papers.abstract: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

papers.title: Sharp Poincaré-Wirtinger Inequalities on Finite Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G_n=(V_{G_n},E_{G_n})$ be the finite connected graph with $n\geq3$ vertices. We study the sharp constant $C_{G_n,p}$ such that the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality \[ \Vert f-m_f\Vert_p\leq C_{G_n,p} {\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}(f) \] holds for every $f$ on $V$, where ${\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}$ stands for the $p$-variation on $G_n$ and $m_f$ stands for the arithmetic mean of $f$. For complete graphs, the optimal constant is known for $p\in[1,3+δ_n^1)\cup(3+δ_n^2,+\infty)$, with $δ_n^1=\frac{1}{2n^2\ln n}+O(1/n^3)$ and $δ_n^2=\frac{2}{n}+O(1/n^2)$. In this paper, we firstly extend the admissible range to all $p\in(0,\infty)$. Secondly, we obtain the sharp constant $C_{S_n,p}$ for the star graph $S_n$ in the range $p\in(0,+\infty)$ and give estimates for the sharp constant $C_{P_n,p}$ on path graphs when $p\in(0,+\infty)$. Thirdly, we characterize the extremizers on complete graphs and star graphs, and establish the existence of monotone extremizers on path graphs for $p\in(0,+\infty)$. For path graphs, we obtain explicit sharp constants for $p\in(0,1]\cup\{2\}$, and interpolation upper bounds for $p\in(1,+\infty)$. We also prove that for any finite connected graph $G_n$, the best constant at $p=+\infty$ is exactly its remoteness. Moreover, for general finite connected graphs $G_n$ and $p\in(0,+\infty)$, we establish optimal bounds for $C_{G_n,p}$; the complete graph uniquely attains the lower bound for all $p>0$; the path graph attains the upper bound for $p>1$, but for $0<p\leq1$ there exist nonpath graphs that attain the same supremum. Finally, we show that our approach yields sharper upper bounds than the path-based estimates obtained via the Cheeger constant.

papers.title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.abstract: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

papers.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
papers.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

papers.title: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix
papers.abstract: While chirality is known to impact chemical and optical properties of molecular systems, as well as their biological function, far less is known about its impact on quantum coherence. By considering a chiral helix as a paradigmatic model, we show that within the Born-Markov regime, changing the degree of helical twist can be used to modulate the electronic decoherence rate. Moderate to strong spin-orbit coupling between next-nearest-neighbor sites along the helix are shown to give rise to a strong dependence of the electronic decoherence rate on the degree of chirality. The effect of chirality on electronic decoherence rates is also seen to be strongly impacted by the spatial and temporal correlations between the local environmental fluctuations to which the local excitations along the helix are subject. Our results show that chirality can serve as a tunable design parameter for quantum engineering and highlight the importance role environmental correlations can play in determining how chirality affects electronic decoherence rates.

papers.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
papers.abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

papers.title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^γ$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^γ$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < γ\leq 1$.

papers.title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
papers.abstract: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-Hölder continuous, where the associated Hölder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.

papers.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
papers.abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.

papers.title: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
papers.abstract: While quantum state exclusion has received considerable attention, the analogous task of measurement outcome exclusion remains less explored. Here we develop a quantitative description of outcome exclusion and extend the resulting framework to obtain necessary and sufficient criteria for measurement simulation by quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing. Our analysis combines two approaches. Algebraic exclusion indices quantify normalized minimum errors in communication tasks with forbidden outputs and yield lower bounds on the number of classical messages required to reproduce the task statistics. Random exclusion profiles provide a statistical description in terms of optimized hypothesis-testing errors and are monotone under both types of processing. This connects outcome exclusion with statistical comparison in the spirit of Blackwell, linking the ability to suppress measurement outcomes to the possibility of simulating one measurement from another.

papers.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
papers.abstract: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

papers.title: A logarithmic saving in the sum-free subset problem
papers.abstract: For every sufficiently large $n$ there is a set of $n$ positive integers, all at most $n^2$, whose largest sum-free subset has size at most $n/3+O(n/\log n)$. We bound the number of small divisible elements in a dense set with few Schur triples. A fixed-accuracy cyclic model gives a rotation, and the original integer triple count controls its density at the required scale.

papers.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
papers.abstract: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. Finally, continuation in $\log q$ produces a logarithmic monodromy whose coefficient is a convergent pairing of the same Borel residues that give the Stokes jump. For the figure-eight knot, the asymptotics of this coefficient are governed by the hyperbolic volume at every rank.

papers.title: Weighted Inequalities for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Trees with Flow Measures
papers.abstract: This paper develops a weighted theory for the fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M_{μ,γ}$, $0<γ<1$, on infinite trees equipped with flow measures. Such measures are typically nondoubling and exhibit exponential volume growth, so the classical Muckenhoupt theory does not apply directly. By replacing Euclidean balls with admissible trapezoids, a class of fractional $A(p,q)(μ)$ weights is introduced, and a Muckenhoupt-type theorem is established: for $1\le p<1/γ$ and $1/p-1/q=γ$, the operator $M_{μ,γ}$ is bounded from $\ell^p_μ(ω^p)$ to $\ell^q_μ(ω^q)$ if and only if $ω\in A(p,q)(μ)$. The endpoint case $p=1$ is characterized via a weak-type estimate.

papers.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
papers.abstract: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this gives an infinite sequence in which the first homology groups have strictly increasing finite orders. All but finitely many members of each sequence admit no complex structure.

papers.title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
papers.abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

papers.title: Volume difference inequalities for central sections of origin-symmetric convex bodies
papers.abstract: Giannopoulos and Koldobsky \cite{GK} asked whether, for origin-symmetric convex bodies $L\subset K\subset\R^n$, the difference $|K|^{(n-k)/n}-|L|^{(n-k)/n}$ is bounded by $C^k$ times the largest difference of their central section volumes in codimension $k$, with a single absolute constant $C$. We prove that the optimal constant $γ_{n,k}$ for fixed $n,k$ satisfies $γ_{n,k}\ge c\sqrt{n/k}$ for an absolute $c>0$. For $k=1$, this lower bound grows as $\sqrt n$ with the dimension, giving a negative answer to the question.

papers.title: The Borel Topos
papers.abstract: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.

papers.title: Stokes corners and the global structure of steady rotating waves in annular domains
papers.abstract: We study steady rotating water waves in a planar annulus, in the model of radial gravity and constant vorticity introduced by Li and the author. The stream function is harmonic, and the free surface carries the Bernoulli condition $p_0^2|\nablaΨ|^2=Q_α(S)$ with $Q_α(R)=(R-r_-)(R-r_+)$. We first settle the crest shape. For $α\neqα_\pm$, every stagnation point lies on the circle $R=r_-$, and the surface forms a symmetric $120^\circ$ corner there. At $α=α_\pm$ the corner is a right angle. The same holds for limits of smooth solutions and, in the lower region, for overhanging waves. We then study the global bifurcation continuum. Its waves are monotone from crest to trough, and they always cross the laminar circle. Hence there is no secondary bifurcation, and the parameter stays above an explicit floor. The continuum ends in an extreme wave, overturns, or degenerates; the last case is excluded for $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$. An annular Nekrasov equation and an invariant Keady--Norbury cone give a slope bound below $90^\circ$ whenever the Nekrasov weight is nonnegative on the waves. A sharpened angular flow-force estimate keeps the troughs where this weight is nonnegative, for every $γ\in(0,1)$ above the floor. Hence, whenever $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$, the existence half of the Stokes conjecture holds: the continuum contains an extreme wave with a $120^\circ$ Stokes crest. In the remaining band $\sinh^2γ<c_0\leγ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$ the result is conditional: the continuum ends in such a wave unless its parameter degenerates to the value at which the effective gravity vanishes on the stagnation circle, and we cannot exclude this degeneration. We also show that the bifurcation is supercritical for every $γ\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
papers.abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).

papers.title: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling. We review the underlying theory, basic experimental findings, and practical methods for the generation, real-time characterization, and active control of soliton families, with a particular focus on recent progress reported for mode-locked fiber-laser platforms. The families covered in the chapter include dissipative solitons, soliton molecules (bound states), and dispersion-managed solitons. For each species, we focus on the pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and emerging intelligent (machine-learning-assisted) control strategies.

papers.title: A short proof of Serre positivity
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.

papers.title: Characterizing $T_0$-spaces where GIS-convergence is topological
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate the GIS-convergence in $T_0$-spaces and the related concept of GIS-continuous spaces(GSI-continuous spaces). It is proved that $SI(X)$ is a locally hypercompact space iff $(X, τ)$ is a $GSI$-continuous space iff GSI-convergence in $X$ with respect to the topology $\mathcal{O}_{SI}(X)$ is topological. We also show that the $GIS$-convergence in $(X, τ)$ is topological if and only if $(X,τ)$ is a $GIS$-continuous space.

papers.title: Gradient-free MCMC exploiting low-dimensional Gaussian and nonGaussian posterior structure
papers.abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order $1/d$. On the posterior axes, the NQU sampler, learning included, needed the fewest evaluations in four of five synthetic examples with $d=200$, among nine baselines including gradient-based ones; in those with non-Gaussian directions, gradient-free baselines needed at least ten times as many. On a methane ignition problem with 219 uncertain rate constants, it gave consistent estimates, whereas full-space robust adaptive Metropolis needed about 300 times as many evaluations and an ensemble sampler degenerated.

papers.title: Wiener-type criteria for parabolic equations with two-sided Gaussian bounds
papers.abstract: We establish sufficient and necessary Wiener-type criteria for boundary regularity of parabolic equations whose fundamental solutions satisfy two-sided Gaussian bounds. In particular, our sufficient criterion holds at the critical exponent in the Gaussian lower bound. For the heat equation, the resulting double-series criterion is equivalent to the classical Wiener criterion of Evans and Gariepy. Our results apply to divergence form equations with bounded measurable, possibly nonsymmetric coefficients, and to non-divergence form equations with coefficients in $\mathrm{DMO}_x$ (Dini mean oscillation in space), without requiring continuity in time.

papers.title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.

papers.title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
papers.abstract: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

papers.title: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems
papers.abstract: The determination of multiple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems is of broad interest in quantum physics. While the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state has been demonstrated in certain specific situations, their universality and exact solvability remain elusive. In this work, we present an exact approach to the double- or triple-excitation dynamics for interacting quantum emitters coupled to environment by deriving a closed equation. By this exact equation, we identify the critical condition for the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state, as well as its relationship to the single-excitation one. Our study not only clearly demonstrates the universality of double- or triple-excitation bound state in open quantum emitter systems, but also reveals the possibility of mediating inter-emitter interactions via multiple-excitation bound states.

papers.title: 10/8-inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary and its application
papers.abstract: As an application of 10/8 inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary, we give criteria of homology 3-spheres represented by certain framed links for having infinite order in the homology cobordism group of homology 3-spheres. Such a class of homology 3-spheres includes certain plumbed 3-manifolds, 1/odd surgeries along certain knots with many twists, for example, certain Montesinos knots, $(p,q)$ cable knots of any knot with some large $p$, $q$, etc.

papers.title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
papers.abstract: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

papers.title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
papers.abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.

papers.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(Γ)$ is edge-transitive, then $Γ$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(Γ)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

papers.title: Modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schrödinger equation with final data $\langle x\rangle^s u_+\in L_x^2,\ d/2<s\le2$, for dimensions $d=1,2,3$, and for both defocusing and focusing cases. We impose no smallness, nonvanishing, or spatial derivative assumption. Most previous modified wave operator results require smallness on $\|\widehat u_+\|_{L^\infty}$, analytic final data or smooth amplitude-phase structure, and the large data modified wave operator problem with finite weighted condition is only solved for 1D defocusing equation. We introduce a new perturbation method which successfully applies to both defocusing and focusing signs when $d\le3$. The main ingredient is an improved growth estimate for the linearized flow, obtained by a low--high frequency decomposition. At low frequencies, spatial localization and freezing the coefficients in space lead to a Fuchsian system. The nilpotent structure at the singular point and a Hamiltonian energy estimate give logarithmic growth for this system. At high frequencies, a modified energy for suitable symmetry operator cancels the leading contribution to energy growth.

papers.title: On equational $\mathfrak{X}$-domains
papers.abstract: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups containing all abelian groups. We introduce and investigate equational $\X$-domains as a generalization of equational domains in algebraic geometry over groups. We characterize these groups by means of systems of equations associated with the identities of $\X$, and describe the radical and coordinate group of the union of two coordinate axes. We also extend classical characterizations of coordinate groups of irreducible algebraic sets, involving discrimination and universal theories, to the setting of equational $\X$-domains. Finally, we establish two construction results: under suitable malnormality, amalgamated free products are equational $\X$-domains; moreover, a restricted regular wreath product of two nontrivial groups is an equational $\X$-domain if and only if its base group is an equational $\X$-domain.

papers.title: Density elimination for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic:a correction and an explicit theory-level completeness proof
papers.abstract: We correct the density-elimination argument for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic in Wang, \emph{Symmetry} 11 (2019), 368, retaining its basic ideas and overall strategy. The published definition of a labelled copy permits independent renamings of antecedent and succedent labels. Under the syntactic splicing interpretation used in that argument, a contraction-free derivable hypersequent and a four-element residuated chain refute the claimed compatibility of the resulting contraction with ordered density elimination. We require a single renaming on both sides of each closed block and prove that the linear rules and coherent closed-block contraction preserve provability of every member of the associated Cartesian families. An occurrence-based separation argument, together with normalization to cuts on the monoidal unit, establishes strong density elimination. We then derive standard completeness from density, retaining the original conclusion for formula theorems. For an explicit Hilbert presentation with independent conjugation parameters, we give a direct relative chain-countermodel proof for arbitrary theories in a countable language. Combined with the full bounded embedding of Wang (2026), this recovers the corresponding strong standard completeness result already stated there. The distinguished constant $f$, when present, is interpreted independently of the monoidal unit and the lattice bounds. The main results of this paper have been formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
papers.abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

papers.title: Asymptotic Normality of the Pearson Correlation between Two Weakly Dependent Random Fields
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the sample Pearson correlation coefficient between two weakly dependent random fields on a lattice of any fixed dimension. Under strict stationarity, $(BL,θ)$-weak dependence and mild moment conditions, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimator on regularly growing domains, which need not be rectangular, with an asymptotic variance expressed through joint fourth-order moments. When the correlation is zero, asymptotic normality holds under weaker conditions. When the fields are independent, the asymptotic variance simplifies to a sum over spatial lags of products of their autocorrelations. The variance approximations behind the classic modified $t$-test, although derived for independent Gaussian fields, target the right variance even without Gaussianity. We also give sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality that are easy to check and cover bounded, Gaussian, $m$-dependent and independent fields. For Gaussian fields, summable auto- and cross-covariances suffice. These conditions rely on new closure results. Squares and products, although not Lipschitz, preserve $(BL,θ)$-dependence for Gaussian fields, and products of independent fields do so when one is positively or negatively associated. Finally, we propose kernel-based estimators of the asymptotic variance, enabling inference without Gaussianity or parametric spatial models. Simulation studies illustrate their finite-sample performance.

papers.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
papers.abstract: The inf-sup constant $β(Ω)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $β$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $β$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $β$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1π$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\leβ\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\leβ\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\leβ\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $β$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $β^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $β$ had been available.

papers.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
papers.abstract: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.

papers.title: Sharp Hellinger Risk of the Multivariate Gaussian NPMLE
papers.abstract: For multivariate Gaussian location mixtures whose mixing distributions have coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails, we prove that the unconstrained nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator attains the minimax rate $(\log n)^d/n$ under squared Hellinger loss. This holds for every fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every fixed tail parameter $σ>0$. The upper bound applies to every measurable choice of a global likelihood maximizer and improves the earlier bound of order $(\log n)^{d+1}/n$ by a factor of $\log n$. A key step is a sharp bracketing bound for multivariate polynomials. For the $L^2(ρ)$ unit ball of real polynomials in $d$ variables with total degree at most $m$, the log bracketing number at width $\varepsilon$ is at most $\binom{m+d}{d}\log(C_d/\varepsilon)$ for $0<\varepsilon\leq1$. The constant $C_d$ depends only on $d$. The bound holds for every positive Borel measure $ρ$ under which each nonzero polynomial in the space has a finite, positive $L^2(ρ)$ norm. We prove the bound using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then apply it to bound the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of Gaussian mixture densities. We obtain the matching minimax lower bound by adapting the Hermite perturbation construction of Kim and Guntuboyina.

papers.title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
papers.abstract: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

papers.title: Cardinal Transfer Events for Infinitary Logic with Infinitary Quantification
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of a certain theory $Φ$, we solve the Gap-$n$ problem for more than one predicate. This will be done for infinitary logic with infinitary quantification.

papers.title: Unit Lattices of Totally Complex, non-CM $D_4$-Octic Number Fields
papers.abstract: Given a number field, we can endow the unit group of its ring of integers, modulo torsion, with the structure of a lattice. Included in the study of the distributions of these lattices is the classification of shapes of unit lattices arising from $D_4$-quartic number fields with signature $(2,1)$. We extend this work to rank 3, by investigating the shapes of lattices arising from the unit groups of totally complex, non-CM $D_4$-octic number fields. In particular, we show all such unit lattices have automorphism group $D_4\times \mathbb{Z}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$, yet none correspond to Gram matrices whose entries are all algebraic.

papers.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.

papers.title: Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles
papers.abstract: The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3πk/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.

papers.title: Phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by a combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum field
papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) driven by non-classical light provides new insights into light-matter interactions and paves the way to quantum attosecond spectroscopy. Achieving phase matching is vital for generating bright HHG sources, while it has received comparatively limited attention in quantum-light-driven HHG. In this work, we investigate the phase matching of HHG driven by an intense coherent field combined with a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) field, using a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi-$Q$ probability distribution. We reveal the physical mechanism behind the distinct pressure dependence of the harmonic yields for odd, even and half-integer sidebands spectral components, as observed in our previous experiment [arXiv:2607.20941]. The simulations and phase-matching model demonstrate that the BSV-induced perturbation of the electron action phase could introduce an additional sub-cycle phase mismatch, such that the amplitude of sub-cycle bursts could be significantly modified by gas pressure after macroscopic propagation, even when the harmonic yield is near the optimum. The resulting amplitude asymmetry of sub-cycle bursts leads to a significant intensity contrast between half-integer sidebands harmonics, manifesting as distinct pressure dependence of their yields. Our findings reveal the phase-matching mechanism in two-color quantum-light-driven HHG, and suggest opportunities for macroscopic control of the non-classical HHG source.

papers.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
papers.abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^β$ Poincaré inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $λ(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-β}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.

papers.title: Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
papers.abstract: The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials. We also discuss behavior of our formulae under connected sums. We give formulations for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of even powers of the Garside element $Δ_3\in B_3$ and a closed formula for the invariant on positive $3$-braids, resulting in a formula for the invariant on all $3$-braids.

papers.title: Rich quantum phase diagram revealed in semimetallic rhombohedral graphene
papers.abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03456-4Previous studies of rhombohedral graphene have focused on a single topological and flat conduction or valence band isolated by strong electric fields. Rhombohedral hexalayer graphene is now found to host various quantum phenomena in the correlated semimetallic regime, featuring symmetry breaking, electric-field-driven band inversion, dual-carrier superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism.

papers.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor
papers.abstract: We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.

papers.title: Variational Thresholds and Multiplicity for a Nonlocal r-Laplacian Logistic-Type Problem
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $λ$: \[ \begin{cases} -Δ_r u - \displaystyle\int_Ω K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +λ|u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_ΩQ(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in Ω, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partialΩ. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $λ$. For $λ\ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(λ<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehatλ^*<λ^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(λ^*<λ<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with positive energy, yielding two distinct nontrivial weak solutions. The same holds at \(λ=λ^*\), where the global minimizer has zero energy. In a left neighborhood of \(λ^*\), two distinct nontrivial weak solutions persist, a local minimizer and a mountain-pass critical point, both with positive energy and the latter at a strictly higher level. For \(λ<\widehatλ^*\), only the trivial solution exists. Finally, as $λ\to 0^-$, the norm of the global minimizers blows up. Along subsequences, selected nonnegative mountain-pass solutions converge strongly in $W_0^{1,r}(Ω)$ as $λ\to 0$ to a nontrivial nonnegative weak solution of the problem at $λ= 0$. The associated mountain-pass levels converge to the same limit from both sides of zero, and the corresponding solution norms also converge to a common value.

papers.title: Counting solutions to Euclidean Fermat equations
papers.abstract: A solution $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^3-\{(0,0,0)\}$ to a Fermat equation \begin{equation} \label{eq:abstract-gfe} Ax^a + By^b + Cz^c = 0 \end{equation} is called \emph{primitive} if $\gcd(x,y,z) = 1$. In the \emph{Euclidean} regime (that is, when the Euler characteristic $χ= \tfrac{1}{a} + \tfrac{1}{b} + \tfrac{1}{c} - 1$ is zero), the equation above defines a smooth genus one curve in a weighted projective plane. We study these models and provide an asymptotic formula for the number of primitive integral solutions with bounded height.

papers.title: Classification of fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system
papers.abstract: We study fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system with four reaction exponents, in which only one component diffuses. For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

papers.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
papers.abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.

papers.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

papers.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
papers.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

papers.title: Equivariant Levi restriction
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $\bbC$, $L\subset G$ a Levi subgroup, and $\cL\subset\cG$ their Langlands duals. Macerato \cite{macerato2023leviequivariantrestrictionsphericalperverse} computed the $\cL(\calO)$-equivariant cohomology of the $!$-restriction to $\GrL$ of the regular spherical perverse sheaf on $\GrG$, and identified it with the functions on the partial Kostant--Whittaker reduction $T^*(G/U,\psiL)$, where $\psiL$ is the possibly degenerate Whittaker character of $U$ determined by $L$. We add loop rotation. Our main result is: the $\LO$-equivariant cohomology of the same object is the ring $\Dh(G/U,\psiL)$ of asymptotic $\psiL$-twisted differential operators on $G/U$. For a single $\IC_V$ the answer is the space of intertwiners $\bM_\hbar(\psiL)\to V\otimes\bM_\hbar(\psiL)$ of the universal Verma--Whittaker module. This interpolates between results of Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg ($L=G$) and Ginzburg--Riche ($L=T$).

papers.title: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schrödinger operator $-\partial_s^2+κ^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4π^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.

papers.title: Semisimple-Unipotent Decomposition and the Exact Order of a Linear Cellular Automaton over F_2
papers.abstract: We study the linear cellular automaton on the cyclic graph $C_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by the local rule $v_i(t+1)=v_{i-1}(t)\oplus v_i(t)\oplus v_{i+1}(t)$ (Wolfram's Rule 150 under periodic boundary conditions). Identifying the configuration space $V_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $R_n = \mathbb{F}_2[x] / \langle x^n - 1 \rangle$, the evolution operator corresponds to multiplication by $G(x)=1+x+x^{n-1}$. We re-derive the invertibility criterion $3\nmid n$, classify periodic and transient behaviour, and prove that Hamming weight is non-monotone for every $n\ge3$. We then factor $x^n-1$ via the Chinese Remainder Theorem and separate semisimple contributions governed by finite-field multiplicative orders from unipotent contributions governed by Frobenius squaring. We determine the exact local unipotent orders and obtain a closed-form global order $r(A)$: $r(A)=2^{m-1}$ for $n=2^m$ with $m\ge2$, while for $n=2^m q$, $q>1$ odd and $3\nmid n$, $r(A)=2^m\operatorname{lcm}(m_2,\ldots,m_r)$. The theory is illustrated by $n=5,7,8,16$ and computationally verified for small dimensions.

papers.title: From invasion to replacement: excursions of the Moran model
papers.abstract: An excursion-theoretic description of the continuous-time Moran model with recurrent mutation is developed. Exploiting its birth--death structure, the killed Moran process is characterized through its Green function, resolvent, Laplace transforms of hitting times, and spectral decomposition. A duality between the Moran model and a pure-death process is also established, yielding a spectral representation of its transition probabilities. The characterization of the killed process leads to a boundary-switching excursion representation in which returning excursions correspond to unsuccessful invasions of an allelic type, whilst switching excursions describe population-wide allelic replacement.
