papers.abstract: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.

papers.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
papers.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

papers.title: Nontrivial Expanding Kähler--Ricci Solitons and Automorphism Groups of Stein Domains
papers.abstract: We study complete nontrivial expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete real holomorphic soliton fields. Let $Ω$ be a relatively compact domain in a complex surface such that a neighborhood of $\overlineΩ$ admits a holomorphic immersion into Euclidean space. We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $Ω$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$. In higher dimensions, we establish existence criteria using the adjoint representation of automorphism groups, boundary geometry, and homogeneous positive closed $(1,1)$-currents. We give sufficient conditions for the holomorphic $\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$-action on the universal globalization of a proper holomorphic $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$-action on a Stein $n$-manifold to be free and proper. Applications include bounded convex and homogeneous domains, domains satisfying weak Kobayashi visibility, and certain finite-type domains.

papers.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
papers.abstract: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

papers.title: Quotient maps, pliability, and Lusin approximation in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In Carnot groups, we show that pliability and the Lusin approximation property are preserved by quotient maps, and we deduce several applications. For instance, we show that, in free Carnot groups of step at least 3 with at least $2$ generators, every horizontal direction is non-pliable, the Lusin property fails in a strong sense, and there is a Lipschitz curve that is purely unrectifiable with respect to smooth horizontal curves. We also give a previously unpublished example of a pliable Carnot group, namely, the group of upper triangular, unipotent matrices.

papers.title: (n-1)-Dimensional Hausdorff Measure Estimates for Free Boundaries of Infinity Laplace Equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric properties of free boundaries associated with nonnegative viscosity solutions to the infinity Laplace equation with strong absorption $$ Δ_\infty u=λu_+^m, \qquad λ>0,\quad 0<m<3. $$ We first establish a sharp distance-to-free-boundary regularity estimate with an explicit optimal coefficient, which coincides with the constant in the non-degeneracy estimate. This exact matching yields a uniform interior tangent ball property at every sufficiently small scale for every free boundary point. As consequences, we obtain a sharp lower density bound of $1/2$ for the positive phase, a locally finite covering of the free boundary by Lipschitz graphs, and quantitative local estimates for its $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the question raised by Araújo, Leitão, and Teixeira (J. Funct. Anal. {\textbf 270} (2016), no. 6, 2249-2267). The underlying barrier mechanism also suggests possible extensions to more general equations.

papers.title: Surfaces of constant sectional curvature in Minkowski space with a canonical semi-symmetric connection
papers.abstract: We study surfaces in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^3_1$ with constant intrinsic sectional curvature with respect to canonical semi-symmetric connections, metric or non-metric, determined by a parallel vector field $\mathcal{V}$. We compute the ambient sectional curvature and obtain a formula for the intrinsic sectional curvature of nondegenerate surfaces in terms of their Gauss and mean curvatures. We provide a complete classification of cylindrical surfaces with constant intrinsic sectional curvature, covering all causal characters of $\mathcal{V}$ and of the rulings. For rotational surfaces whose axes are parallel to $\mathcal{V}$, we reduce the constant-curvature condition to an ordinary differential equation. Explicit solutions are obtained for null axes and, in the metric case, for surfaces with zero intrinsic sectional curvature.

papers.title: Symmetries, conservation laws, series solutions and singularity formation for the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations in mass coordinates
papers.abstract: Written in Lagrangian mass coordinates, the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations for a polytropic gas become a single second-order equation for the radius $r(t,m)$ of the shell enclosing mass $m$, with adiabatic index $γ>1$ and entropy profile $S(m)$. We determine all point symmetries of this equation. Apart from time translation there is at most one scaling, except at the critical index $γ=4/3$, where a scaling exists for every entropy profile; these scalings are the entropy-fixed stabilisers of the two-parameter scaling group of the non-isentropic system, and we give the exact symmetry defect when $γ\neq4/3$. Noether's theorem singles out the profiles $S=Km^{14-10γ}$, for which a scaling is variational and gives a conservation law beyond energy; otherwise the scalings yield virial identities. We construct exact collapse solutions and reduce the self-similar problem to one ordinary differential equation. Using the Briot-Bouquet theorem we prove that the regular centre of self-similar and homologous collapse carries a convergent analytic expansion with free central amplitude, and we derive a Puiseux expansion at the stellar surface whose exponent is the polytropic index $1/(γ-1)$. In mass coordinates a density singularity is a zero of $r_m$ or of $r$; for the first kind we prove a Hopf-type fold law and an exact shell-crossing criterion for free-falling dust. Finally, linear perturbations of the critical Einstein-de Sitter collapse separate exactly into spherical Bessel profiles, with exponents solving $3κ^2+κ-2+μ=0$. All identities were checked by computer algebra, and the numerical statements rest on convergence studies of a second-order Lagrangian scheme, including a collapse with a free surface.

papers.title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
papers.abstract: Organizations use large language models (LLMs) to classify jobs that differ in uncertainty and the cost of errors. Querying additional models may improve accuracy, but it also incurs fees and increases congestion at shared servers. We study congestion-aware adaptive routing (CAAR) policies that adapt model selection and stopping decisions to observed outputs while accounting for the steady-state congestion they generate. The objective is to minimize the long-run average cost of misclassification penalties, query fees, and holding costs. We can represent CAAR policies as a mixture of decision trees, and derive exact holding costs for first-come-first-served servers with exponential service times and processor-sharing servers with general service times. We formulate a convex optimization problem with unique optimal model loads. Congestion prices capture the marginal system-wide holding costs of additional queries and guide routing and stopping decisions through a Bayesian dynamic program. We characterize optimal stopping decisions and identify models whose information does not justify their cost. A column-generation algorithm computes optimal CAAR policies and provides an explicit optimality-gap bound. We also bound the additional cost of limiting cascade depth relative to full-depth CAAR. Finally, under a common query-depth limit, cascades with a predetermined model order can be arbitrarily more costly than optimal CAAR, even when the order is randomized and stopping decisions adapt to observed outputs. Numerical experiments distinguish the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design.

papers.title: Quantum Approximation and Integration in Sobolev Spaces -- Low Smoothness
papers.abstract: We study the complexity of approximation and integration in Sobolev spaces in the quantum setting of information-based complexity theory (IBC). Previous results have been obtained under the assumption that the embedding condition holds. Here we drop this assumption and use a quantum version of a previously developed stochastic discretization technique.

papers.title: The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles
papers.abstract: We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.

papers.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.

papers.title: Gibbs-type allelic partitions of $Λ$-coalescents: a rigidity theorem
papers.abstract: Let $Π^θ_n$ be the allelic partition induced by a $Λ$-coalescent with mutation rate $θ$ under the infinitely-many-alleles model. We characterise the finite measures $Λ$ for which the EPPF of $Π^θ_n$ is of Gibbs type: the only possibility is $Λ=c\,δ_0$, corresponding to Kingman's coalescent and the Ewens sampling formula. Starting from Möhle's recursion, we derive its EPPF form and organise the Gibbs constraints by the difference between sample size and number of blocks. The first two sectors yield identities valid for every $Λ$; the next gives a scalar obstruction and a forward recursion for the Hausdorff moments of $Λ$. Complete monotonicity settles the zero-index case, while positive indices are excluded by an exact polynomial-positivity certificate at sample size six. Consequently, every non-Kingman allelic law fails the standard Gibbs factorisation on a sample of size six. We also derive asymptotic obstructions under regular variation and study product-beta merger measures and finite-sample departures from Gibbs form.

papers.title: Roman-Type Domination on Bisplit Graphs: Hardness and Inapproximability
papers.abstract: Inspired by the structure and name of split graphs, bisplit graphs have three independent sets $I,A,B$, where every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, and vertices of $I$ may have arbitrary neighborhoods in the core $A\cup B$. Thus they have a complete bipartite core together with the remaining vertices, making them a structured setting in which to study how core size affects complexity. Mann and Fernau's construction already implies NP-completeness of perfect Roman domination on bisplit graphs with a singleton core side \citep[Theorem~20]{mann-fernau-pr}. Motivated by this result, we study all four Roman-type domination problems across further core-size regimes: we prove NP-completeness when one core side has size one or two, and when both sides have size at least three. For perfect Italian domination, even deciding whether prescribed core labels of total weight two can be extended is NP-complete on bipartite bisplit graphs. Approximation is also addressed: for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation exists for perfect Roman domination when one core side has fixed size $1$, $2$, or $3$, or for perfect Italian domination on bipartite bisplit graphs whose two core sides grow with the input. All four problems are fixed-parameter tractable for both parameters. Given supplied modulators of size $k$, the running-time bases, in the order Roman, perfect Roman, Italian, and perfect Italian, are $4,11,11,18$ for cluster vertex deletion and $6,11,11,18$ for biclique-cluster vertex deletion, up to polynomial factors. The $4^k$ Roman cluster-deletion bound is known; the other bounds follow from our dynamic programs. To our knowledge, the latter parameter has not previously been studied explicitly for domination variants.

papers.title: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
papers.abstract: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

papers.title: Sharpness of the Brjuno Condition for Hyperbolic Bishop Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $μ\in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|μ|=1$, and assume that $μ$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_γ$ denote the Bishop quadric with $γ= 1/\sqrt{2+μ+μ^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $μ$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_γ$. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Convergence of potential-preserving annealed Sinkhorn algorithm
papers.abstract: The annealed Sinkhorn algorithm is an iterative method for approximating solutions of optimal transport problems, in which the entropic regularisation parameter is progressively decreased. As this parameter decreases, one may preserve either the multiplicative scaling factors or the corresponding dual potentials. We study the potential-preserving iterates under positive, non-increasing regularisation schedules tending to zero. We prove that, if the schedule is non-summable, the iterates admit a subsequence converging to a solution of the corresponding optimal transport problem. The non-summability condition is sharp, as for every summable schedule in this class we construct an example in which the iterates converge to a plan violating the prescribed source marginal. We further establish convergence of the entire sequence if the relative inverse-temperature increments are also square-summable, and show by example that non-summability alone does not guarantee full convergence. Our convergence conditions are satisfied by linear inverse-temperature schedules, under which recent work has shown that the scaling-preserving iterates fail to converge to a solution of the optimal transport problem. We also derive convergence rates for polynomial inverse-temperature schedules up to and including linear growth, extending the marginal KL bound obtained by mirror-descent analysis at fixed temperature. Our best rate for the transport cost gap after rounding improves on that established for scaling-preserving annealing. Simple numerical illustrations accompany these convergence results.

papers.title: Automorphisms Induced on Cartan Tori and Centers of Quantized Enveloping Algebras
papers.abstract: Let \(U=U_q(\mathfrak g)\) be the root-lattice form of the quantized enveloping algebra associated with a complex simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), over a field \(\mathbb{k}\) of characteristic zero, with \(q\in\mathbb{k}^{\times}\) not a root of unity. We determine the groups of automorphisms induced by algebra automorphisms of $U$ on its Cartan torus $U^0$ and its center $Z(U)$. These groups are \[ \Aut_U(U^0)\cong\Hom(Q,\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Aut(Φ), \] \[ \Aut_U(Z(U))\cong\Hom((P/Q)[2],\{\pm1\})\rtimesΓ, \] where $Q$ and $P$ are the root and weight lattices, $Φ$ is the root system, $Γ$ is the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak g$, and $(P/Q)[2]$ is the $2$-torsion subgroup of $P/Q$. The proof uses characters of finite-dimensional modules and Weyl-group invariant fields to show that the automorphism of $Q$ determined by the toral restriction preserves $Φ$. Writing $ρ_0$ and $ρ_Z$ for the restriction maps to $U^0$ and $Z(U)$, respectively, we prove that $\kerρ_0\subseteq\kerρ_Z$ and determine the quotient $\kerρ_Z/\kerρ_0$.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
papers.abstract: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.

papers.title: Existence and nonexistence of global solutions to a semilinear parabolic equation with variable reaction on sub-Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t-Δ_{\mathcal{M}}u=h(t)[f(u)]^{p(x)}$ on $\mathcal{M}\times(0,T)$, with $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in L^q(\mathcal{M})$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is a complete sub-Riemannian manifold endowed with a smooth volume measure and $Δ_{\mathcal{M}}$ denotes the associated sub-Laplacian. The function $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty))$, $f$ is nonnegative and continuous, and $p$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathcal{M}$. We establish sharp criteria for the existence and nonexistence of nonnegative global solutions. In particular, our framework applies to connected unimodular Lie groups, yielding global existence, nonexistence, and Fujita-type results. Our approach allows for nonlinearities $f$ beyond the convex setting, thereby broadening the scope of earlier nonexistence results in the Euclidean framework. Furthermore, our results generalize those of Ruzhansky and Yessirkegenov, whose analysis relies on polynomial-type bounds of the form $K_1u^p\le f(u)\le K_2u^p$ with fixed constants $K_1,K_2>0$ and $p>1$.

papers.title: Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using Quantum Devices: QUBO and HOBO Formulations
papers.abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) forms the foundation for many logistics and optimization tasks. At the same time, this problem is NP-hard and requires significant computational resources. Quantum computing promises to substantially accelerate computations or increase solution accuracy. The TSP can be conveniently mapped onto the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulation, which in turn can be solved using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) methods, but this mapping requires a quadratic number of qubits. The higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) formulation requires significantly fewer qubits, but it contains higher-order terms. In our work, we thoroughly investigate both formulations and provide a practical recipe for solving the TSP. We give a comprehensive study and compare in detail QUBO and HOBO formulations.

papers.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
papers.abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

papers.title: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: A conjectured refinement of the Lieb--Solovej inequality at Rényi order one half
papers.abstract: We conjecture that the Wigner logarithmic negativity of any single-mode state is bounded by the amount by which the Rényi-$1/2$ entropy of its Husimi function exceeds the coherent-state value, with equality only for coherent states. If true, this refines the Lieb--Solovej (generalized Wehrl) inequality with a remainder term that is a resource monotone, and it implies that heterodyne statistics alone certify an upper bound on the classical-simulation cost of a state. We show that it suffices to prove the conjecture for pure states, since the negativity is convex and the squared $L^{1/2}$ norm of the Husimi function is concave. We prove the conjecture up to an additive constant $\ln 2$ for all states, and identify where the factor of two is lost: For pure states the Wigner function is the wavefunction of a two-mode state obtained by passive operations, and over generic two-mode wavefunctions our constant is already optimal, so that a proof of the sharp bound must exploit the product structure of that state. Finally, we show with an explicit superposition of the vacuum and a distant coherent state that the analogous inequality fails for the Wehrl entropy and for higher Rényi orders, meaning that the conjecture is not a consequence of the majorization relation underlying the Lieb--Solovej theorem.

papers.title: $C^{m,α}$-rectifiability in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In an arbitrary Carnot group $\mathbb{G}$ of homogeneous dimension $Q$, we characterize rectifiability of sets of finite Hausdorff measure by $\mathbf C_{\mathbb{G}}^{m,α}$-regular surfaces with complemented vertical tangent subgroups, for every $m\ge1$ and $α\in[0,1]$. The criterion combines positive lower density with approximation in measure by tubes around such surfaces. At almost every point, one tube radius $λr^{m+α}$ suffices for $α>0$, whereas the estimate must hold for every $λr^m$, $λ>0$, for $α=0$. Tubular approximation upgrades $\mathbf C^1_{\mathbb{G}}$-rectifiability to class $(m,α)$ without an additional density assumption. The proof combines ambient normal-form polynomial jets, a Remez-type norming inequality, and Whitney extension. In topological dimension at least two, quantitative volume approximation by noncharacteristic sublevel sets yields higher-order rectifiability of reduced boundaries. In particular, for weak solutions of the horizontal Poisson equation with $L^q_{\mathrm{loc}}$ forcing ($q>\max\{Q,2\}$ finite), almost every sublevel set has second-order rectifiable reduced boundary.

papers.title: Global $C^{2,α}$ Estimates for Complex $k$-Hessian Equations on Kähler Manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori $C^{2,α}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side.

papers.title: Three commuting matrices whose lifts never commute
papers.abstract: We construct pairwise commuting matrices over $\mathbb{F}_p$ which have no pairwise commuting lifts to $\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z}$. Equivalently, there are mod $p$ representations of the absolute Galois group of the field of iterated Laurent series $\mathbb{C}((x_1))\cdots((x_d))$ which do not lift modulo $p^2$.

papers.title: Unified Schur multiple zeta functions
papers.abstract: We define symmetric multiple zeta values, unified zeta functions, and finite zeta values in the Schur setting. We establish a Jacobi--Trudi formula and a Giambelli formula for unified Schur multiple zeta functions, and we show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between finite and symmetric Schur multiple zeta values under the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture. We also show a vanishing property for a symmetric sum of finite Schur multiple zeta values, generalizing a result obtained by Hoffman for finite multiple zeta values.

papers.title: Smooth Exterior Potentials for a Gradient-Weighted Hessian Equation
papers.abstract: We construct a positive solution of an exterior Dirichlet problem for a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian operator on each smooth strictly star-shaped domain whose boundary curvatures lie in $Γ_k$. For $p>1$ sufficiently close to one, the solution is smooth up to the boundary, has no critical points, and is unique among continuous potentials on the natural viscosity branch. Its levels remain strictly star-shaped and strictly $k$-convex. We determine its radial asymptotics through two derivatives and the uniform limit of $(p-1)|Du_p|$ on the boundary. The construction perturbs an inverse curvature-quotient flow. In logarithmic radial coordinates the exact equation is elliptic for $p>1$ and its limit is parabolic. A weighted inverse estimate on the half-cylinder controls the singular perturbation.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.

papers.title: A discontinuous Galerkin method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we have analysed a discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for the coupled surface-subsurface flow, which is modelled by the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy (NSD) equations. While the DG method has been applied for the spatial discretization of both Navier-Stokes and Darcy equations, for time, we have employed the first-order backward Euler scheme. The fully discrete error analysis has been carried out for both velocity and pressure of the Navier-Stokes equations, and for the piezometric head of the Darcy equation, and optimal estimates have been derived. Our analysis relies on appropriate treatments of the nonlinear convective term from the Navier-Stokes equations, along with the interface conditions that couple the system. We have employed a modified Oseen operator on an appropriate DG setup along with the standard duality argument to derive optimal error estimates in the L2-norm for the unknowns, which are novel for the NSD equations within the DG framework and are supported by numerical simulations demonstrating the scheme's efficiency.

papers.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to LR B-Splines
papers.abstract: We review the theoretical foundations of locally refined (LR) B-splines, a natural extension of univariate B-splines to multivariate, locally refined, and generally unstructured box partitions. LR B-splines are defined using standard tools from B-spline theory, such as knot insertion, and retain key properties including locality, non-negativity, and a piecewise polynomial structure. Our presentation starts from the definition of spline spaces over box partitions and discusses the instability of their dimension formula due to the presence of a homological term. Conditions ensuring the stabilization of the dimension naturally motivate the construction of LR meshes and LR B-splines. We subsequently analyze the spanning properties of LR B-splines, with particular emphasis on completeness, linear dependence, and local linear independence. We also address known characterizations and refinement strategies ensuring that the resulting LR B-splines preserve the desirable properties of tensor-product B-splines.

papers.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
papers.abstract: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $π_v/β_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(π_v/β_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.

papers.title: Probabilistic well-posedness of dispersive PDEs beyond variance blowup II: quadratic nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We study the quadratic nonlinear wave equation (NLW), posed on the two-dimensional torus, with rough Gaussian random initial data beyond the variance blowup threshold observed by Okamoto and the fourth author (2021). By introducing a suitable vanishing multiplicative renormalization constant on the frequency-truncated Gaussian random initial data, we prove that the corresponding solutions converge in law to a solution to the stochastic NLW with zero initial data, driven by a Gaussian space-time noise whose temporal covariance at each spatial Fourier mode is given by the Bessel function of order $0$. We also show that the solution to the limiting equation almost surely blows up in a finite time, and that the convergence above holds on every compact time interval before the maximal existence time. %on the maximal time of existence. A main new ingredient is the analysis of the oscillatory covariance of the second Picard iterates. We identify the limiting covariance by averaging the leading oscillatory phase over the angular variable. In contrast to our previous work on the Benjamin-Bona-Mahony equation (2025), multilinear dispersive smoothing plays an essential role both in proving tightness of the second Picard iterates and in controlling the rough nonlinear interactions via paracontrolled analysis. The resulting gain of a quarter of a derivative persists in the limit, where it is reflected in the decay of the Bessel covariance.

papers.title: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses
papers.abstract: Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours. Here, we replace conventional square control pulses with two drift-resilient pulse families: the adiabatic BIR-4 and the composite CORPSE. In a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device, we benchmark single-qubit gate sets built from each pulse against deliberate miscalibration. We find that BIR-4 offers a 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor of 2 change in drive power and CORPSE maintains similar fidelity over +/-0.9MHz of offset. When fully calibrated CORPSE offers a 99.97% fidelity per gate, on par with a calibrated square pulse. Starting with tuned pulses, we then track errors using gate-set tomography for ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees throughout, including across a 1.3MHz frequency jump. Our results demonstrate that these pulses can maintain high-fidelity operations without constant recalibration, mitigating the need for constant tuning, which is a key bottleneck in scaling quantum-dot-based quantum processors.

papers.title: Quartic hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{A}^3$ isomorphic to the affine plane
papers.abstract: In 1975 Abhayankar and Moh have shown that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 all polynomial embeddings of the affine line into the affine plane are equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. For embeddings of the affine plane into $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose image is a hypersurface of degree 3, it is shown in arXiv:1912.02144 that they are also equivalent to the standard embedding as a hyperplane. We will consider the case where the image is a quartic hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ and classify all such hypersurfaces up to affine automorphisms.

papers.title: Codimension two complements in hyperbolic products
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-volume locally symmetric manifold modeled on $\H^m \times \H^n$, and let $S$ be a compact, totally geodesic, codimension two submanifold of $M$ modeled on $\H^{m-1} \times \H^{n-1}$. In this paper, we initiate the study of manifolds of the form $N = M \setminus S$. In the case where $M$ is a product and $S$ is connected, we prove that such $N$ admit complete, finite-volume, $A$-regular metrics with non-positive sectional curvature. We also deduce some topological properties of $N$, and algebraic properties of $π_1(N)$. In the case where $M$ is irreducible, we show that $N$ admits {\it almost non-positive curvature}. Similar results hold for manifolds $X_d$, which are $d$-fold branched covers of $M$ ramified over $S$. Along the way, we show that there are infinitely many commensurability classes of such pairs $(M,S)$, and develop general curvature formulas for doubly warped product metrics, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Closed-Form Formula for $d_{\mathrm{critical}}(a_0)$ in Large Fully Connected Power Grids
papers.abstract: Kadloor and Santhi (arXiv:1011.4098) modeled cascading failures in a large fully connected power grid by a coupled four-variable recursion for the minimum surviving load $a_n$, the mean failed load $μ_{n-1}$, the redistributed load $\mathcal{D}_n$, and the stagewise failure probability $p_n$. They noted that the recursion was not tractable and identified the critical disturbance $d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ by simulation. We show that the recursion telescopes exactly into a one-dimensional monotone map $a_{n+1} = g(a_n)$. This yields the threshold in closed form: $1 - a_0 = d_{\mathrm{critical}}\,(1 + \ln(1 + 1/d_{\mathrm{critical}}))$, or explicitly in terms of the lower branch $W_{-1}$ of the Lambert W function. We prove a sharp dichotomy. For $d_m \le d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ the cascade halts with limiting load $a_0 + d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ at criticality and surviving fraction $1/(1 + d_{\mathrm{critical}})$. For $d_m > d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ a complete outage occurs in finitely many steps.

papers.title: Why $(4x(1-x))^{3/4}$ approximates the binary entropy so well: a proof of Topsøe's convexity conjecture
papers.abstract: Write the binary entropy as $h(x) = u^{g(x)}$ with $u = 4x(1-x)$. Topsoe (2001) proved the sharp bounds $1/\ln 4 \le g \le 1$, i.e. $u \le h \le u^{1/\ln 4}$, and conjectured that the effective exponent $g$ is convex. We prove this conjecture. In the variable $s = (1-2x)^2$, $g$ extends to a Pick function on $\mathbb{C} \setminus [1,\infty)$ with an explicit positive density on the cut, so that $g(x) = \sum_n γ_n (1-2x)^{2n}$ with $γ_n > 0$ and $(γ_n)_{n \ge 1}$ a moment sequence. Pinelis's monotonicity theorem, Topsoe's power-type bounds and the optimality of their exponents follow as corollaries, together with a classification of all exponents $α$ for which $u^α$ bounds $h$. The proof is by hand except for one inequality in one real variable on a bounded interval, certified by interval arithmetic. As an application we give sharp, certified constants for the approximation $h \approx u^{3/4}$: $-0.0065493 \le u^{3/4} - h \le 0.0080004$ on $[0,1]$.

papers.title: Higher-Order Minkowski Inequalities via Gradient-Weighted Hessian Potentials
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp boundary inequality for exterior potentials of a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian equation under regularity, level-curvature, flux conservation, and radial decay hypotheses. The inequality bounds a power of the Newton flux by the normalized integral of $H_k^p/H_{k-1}^{p-1}$, and equality characterizes balls. After a conformal change of metric, two Newton-tensor divergence identities give comparisons between regular levels even when the slab between them contains critical points. For smooth strictly star-shaped domains with strictly $k$-convex boundary, a companion existence theorem supplies exterior potentials for $p$ close to one. We identify the limiting flux with the integral of $H_{k-1}$ and recover the sharp consecutive Minkowski inequality, including its equality case.

papers.title: The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces
papers.abstract: We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{N,s}$ such that for every measurable set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of finite positive measure, $$ \sup\Bigl\{\frac{1}{|Ω|}\int_Ωe^{α_{s,N}|u|^{\frac{p}{p-1}}}dx: u\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^N), u=0\text{ a.e. on }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΩ, [u]_{s,p}\le 1\Bigr\}\le C_{N,s}, $$ where $[u]_{s,p}$ is the Gagliardo seminorm and $α_{s,N}$ is the upper threshold found by Parini and Ruf for $N\ge 2$ and by Iula for $N=1$. Moreover, the constant $α_{s,N}$ is sharp. This answers two of their questions. We use a nonlocal version of Moser's one-dimensional lemma. The $p$-th moment of a translation kernel on the logarithmic half-line determines the sharp coefficient, and finiteness of the next moment characterizes the endpoint. We obtain sharp singular, whole-space, Adachi--Tanaka type, concentration-compactness and affine inequalities. When the Euclidean distance in the seminorm is replaced by the gauge of an origin-symmetric star body $K$, we determine the sharp exponent for each fixed $K$ and show that it exceeds the volume-normalized exponent unless $K$ is an ellipsoid. The same exponents are sharp for regional seminorms on bounded Lipschitz domains in dimensions $N\ge 2$. We prove attainment of the critical supremum on balls for $N\ge 2$ and $s$ close to one. In the Hilbert case $N=1$, $s=1/2$, we compute the concentration level of the singular problem on an interval using a sharp weighted logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Consequently, the critical supremum is attained for every singular weight $|x|^{λ-1}$, $0 < λ\le 1$.

papers.title: Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.

papers.title: A Classification of Low Genus Modular Curves
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an open subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\in G$. Associated to $G$, there is a modular curve $X_G$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ which parametrizes elliptic curves with $G$-level structure. We give a classification of modular curves with genus equal to a fixed nonnegative integer $g$. In particular, we show that all modular curves of genus $g$ lie in finitely many families of $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}}$-twists of modular curves. We also describe an algorithm for computing all families of modular curves of a fixed genus $g$ and use this to compute projective models for these modular curves. This algorithm has been fully implemented for $g \leq 12$. In an appendix with Yongyuan Huang and Rakvi, we describe two algorithms, one for computing rational functions on modular curves given as quotients of two modular forms of the same weight, and the other for computing models for the generic fibers of universal elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}_G$, where $G\subset \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an open subgroup satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\notin G$.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of doubly stochastic matrices in large orders
papers.abstract: For $1\le k\le N$, every point in the convex hull of the $k$th roots of unity is an eigenvalue of some doubly stochastic matrix of order $N$. Perfect and Mirsky asked whether any other eigenvalues occur. We prove that the union of these polygons is the whole region for every $N\ge450$. Our pencil-and-paper proof for $N\ge10^{30}$ starts with an eigenvector $v$ of Euclidean norm one. Place one unit of mass at each coordinate $v_j$. If $Av=zv$, row $i$ draws mass $A_{ij}$ from each mark $v_j$, so the mass it receives has centre $zv_i$. The column sums ensure that each mark supplies one unit in total. It follows that the sum of the row variances is $1-|z|^2$. Since the regular $N$-gon contains the disk of radius $\cos(π/N)$, an eigenvalue outside the polygons would force this sum below $\sin^2(π/N)$. We use this bound to compare permutations of the outer marks and to follow a randomly chosen mark through a quarter turn. To reach $450$, we count marks between concentric circles and verify a finite set of inequalities by computer. We also determine the regions in orders five and six by computer-assisted proofs. At order five the full region is obtained by adding to the polygons the segments from the origin to two conjugate arcs traced by roots of quartic polynomials. At order six the square, pentagon and hexagon give the whole region.

papers.title: Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, \varphi_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $\varphi_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.

papers.title: The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs
papers.abstract: By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $α^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $α\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $α^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products
papers.abstract: For a positive semidefinite matrix $X$, let $μ_k(X)$ be the minimum of the least eigenvalues of its principal submatrices of order $k$. For positive semidefinite $A,B$ of order $n$, we prove \[ μ_{i+j-1}(A\circ B)\geqμ_i(A)μ_j(B), \qquad i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\},\quad i+j-1\leq n, \] and characterize equality when the right-hand side is positive. The resulting symmetric least-eigenvalue bound \[ λ_{\min}(A\circ B)\geq \max_{1\leq i\leq n}μ_i(A)μ_{n-i+1}(B) \] recovers the classical Schur lower bounds at endpoint choices and can be exact even when both factors are singular. It is incomparable with the projection bound from a recent companion paper, and combining the two bounds can improve on both. The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $μ_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. Multifactor and Khatri--Rao consequences are also given.

papers.title: The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.

papers.title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
papers.abstract: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.

papers.title: The Exact Value of the Rankin Number gamma_{5,2}
papers.abstract: The Rankin number gamma_{5,2} measures the exact upper bound for the squared determinant of the densest 2-dimensional sublattice of any 5-dimensional lattice of determinant one. We prove that gamma_{5,2}=16^{1/5}, attained by D*_5.

papers.title: Coherent Recovery of Nested Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel Using Erasure Decoding and Quantization
papers.abstract: Motivated by quantum capacity results, we revisit nested binary linear codes for the quantum erasure channel through a packing-covering viewpoint: the outer code supports erasure reconstruction, while the inner code performs erasure quantization. We turn this perspective into two explicit decoder architectures. Architecture I requires no stabilizer-syndrome measurements and combines a classical peeling decoder and erasure quantizer with corresponding coherent quantum reconstruction and cleanup operations that disentangle the logical state from inaccessible erasure-environment branches. Architecture II goes one step further and implements erasure belief propagation directly through reversible ternary quantum gates, providing quantum state healing that reconstructs erased symbols while leaving unerased code states unperturbed. We establish sufficient conditions for exact recovery of arbitrary logical states, and illustrate both architectures using the Steane code, including explicit scheduling procedures and coherent quantum circuits.

papers.title: Wigner Matrices and the $α$-Determinant
papers.abstract: For a Hermitian Wigner matrix $M_n$ and complex $α$ with $|α|\leq1$, we study the $α$-characteristic polynomial $\det_α(zI-M_n)$, which interpolates between the characteristic polynomial ($α=-1$) and the permanental polynomial ($α=1$). Assuming finite fourth moments off the diagonal and second moments on it, we show that this polynomial, normalized by its expectation, converges in distribution off the segment $\sqrt{-α}\,[-2,2]$ to the Wick exponential of an explicit Gaussian analytic function, with the same Gaussian modes for every $α$. As consequences, all zeros lie near this segment with probability tending to one, the empirical zero measure converges to a rotated semicircle law, and analytic linear statistics of the zeros satisfy a central limit theorem. We also show that $\det_α(zI-M_n)$ is approximated, with vanishing relative error, in terms of the characteristic polynomial of $M_n$ at a transformed point. The proof writes the $α$-characteristic polynomial as a polymer gas, which becomes asymptotically ideal after an exact resummation over matchings.

papers.title: Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=Ω(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$. The lower bound improves the exponential base $(9/5)^{1/4}=1.15829\ldots$ of Körner and Marton. It comes from a random system of overlapping local constraints, in which every position is read two or three times, followed by thinning and the deletion of nearby pairs and of the remaining triples that violate trifference. The required estimates reduce to finitely many inequalities, which we verify rigorously by computer. The upper bound improves our earlier bound $O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)$.

papers.title: Trace-class perturbations of Voiculescu's free semicircular families
papers.abstract: Let $\{s_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ be the standard free semicircular family on the full Fock space $\mathcal H=\mathcal F(\ell^2(Λ))$, where $|Λ|\geqslant2$. For any family $\{K_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ of self-adjoint trace-class operators with $γ=\sum_{j\inΛ}\|K_j\|_1<\infty$, we prove that the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand $\mathcal P$ of the von Neumann algebra $W^*(\{s_j+K_j\colon j\inΛ\})$ is isomorphic to the free group factor $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_Λ)$. As an application, we show that the set of irreducible operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not dense in the trace-class norm. For each fixed $γ>0$, the possible values of the Murray--von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal P}(z_{\mathcal P}\mathcal H)$ form the interval $[1,1+γ)$, where $z_{\mathcal P}$ is the identity of $\mathcal P$.

papers.title: Strong Subdifferentiability in Bochner Function spaces $L^{p}(μ, X)$
papers.abstract: In this article, for $1\leq p<\infty$, we provide a characterization of strongly subdifferentiable points of $L^{p}(μ, X)$, when $X^*$ is separable and $μ$ is the Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$. For $f\in L^{p}(μ, X)$ with $\|f\|_{p}=1$ we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferetiable at $f$ if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable at $f(t)$ for almost every \(t\in[0,1]\) with $f(t)\neq 0$. Moreover, for a separable Banach space $X$, we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferentiable if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable.

papers.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.

papers.title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
papers.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
papers.abstract: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $Δ(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.

papers.title: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
papers.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

papers.title: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

papers.title: Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ<γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ=γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $γ_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.

papers.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
papers.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $σ$-local compactness, $σ$-compactness, the Lindelöf property, and left $ω$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindelöf property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

papers.title: Lessons from Chess: Mathematics in the Age of AI
papers.abstract: The history of chess offers a perspective on the growing role of artificial intelligence in mathematics. We explore the parallels and limitations of this analogy and consider possible directions for mathematical research, education, and the public perception of mathematics.

papers.title: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
papers.abstract: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_δ$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

papers.title: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
papers.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

papers.title: Strong Banach property $(T)$ for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$
papers.abstract: Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
papers.abstract: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ is of class $k$. $\boldsymbol{4}$. For generic $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^k$, $Σ_{Q}$ contains $\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$ collections of ellipsoids of codimension $2$ consisting of degenerate parabolic points. $\boldsymbol{5}$. If $k>\ell$, the parabolic set in $Σ_{Q}$ (if any) is a union of hyperplane closed discs bounded by ellipsoids. $\boldsymbol{6}$. The above ellipsoids (items $4$ and $5$) are in bijection with the isolated singular points in $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$.

papers.title: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Ampère equation
papers.abstract: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Ampère density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(Ω)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(Ω\).

papers.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact Kähler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact Kähler manifolds.

papers.title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
papers.abstract: We introduce a geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation for the $L^2$-gradient flow of a class of curvature-dependent energies of closed hypersurfaces, where the energy density depends on the mean curvature and the unit normal. A square-root auxiliary variable converts the geometric energy into a quadratic functional. Combining its evolution equation with a skew-symmetric treatment of surface transport yields a weak formulation whose energy law depends only on the normal velocity and is therefore independent of the chosen tangential motion. We construct monolithic nonlinear parametric finite element methods by coupling a common IEQ discretization with one of two geometric formulations that accommodate either the Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) tangential velocity or the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential velocity. Both fully discrete approximations satisfy an unconditional decay estimate for the discrete quadratic energy. We further extend the construction to anisotropic Willmore flow, and to $H^{-1}$-gradient flows. A variety of numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the introduced methods.

papers.title: On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms
papers.abstract: In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.

papers.title: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions
papers.abstract: Let $κ$ be $λ$-supercompact for a regular $λ>κ$. We show that if $λ$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $κ$, $\diamondsuit(S^λ_{\geqκ})$ implies that every ${<}κ$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $λ$ is a projection of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $κ$-distributive projections of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $κ$-distributive forcings of size $λ$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.

papers.title: Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent
papers.abstract: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $π$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.

papers.title: Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors
papers.abstract: We report a broadband optical delay line programmable for delays up to 1 μs with nanosecond resolution, while preserving an arbitrary and unknown polarization state of the original light. The delay line comprises bidirectional pass in cascaded segments of standard single-mode fibers, along with terminal reflection from Faraday mirrors (FMs) at both ends. Each segment contains either a short path or a long path, selected by an optical switch. The FMs auto-compensate for random polarization fluctuations introduced by the optical fibers, thereby restoring the initial polarization state. Broadband operation of the delay line was assessed by investigating dispersion of both the fiber and the FMs. Surprisingly, we found that the two-pass propagation in the fiber can mitigate dispersive distortion introduced by the FM. Numerical experiments demonstrated that the output polarization state of the delay line has a mean fidelity better than 99% over a range of 50-nm deviation from the central wavelength. Remarkably, the mean fidelity often surpasses that in the absence of the fiber itself.

papers.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.abstract: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

papers.title: Reflected Elastic Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. A key analytical ingredient, of independent interest, is a pair of moment asymptotics, as $t\downarrow 0$, for the boundary local time of a reflected diffusion, extending known results for the unreflected case. Uniqueness in law of $\widetilde X$ among Feller REDs sharing the same interior dynamics is established through a resolvent/boundary-value-problem argument. The result extends the classical Itô-McKean construction of elastic Brownian motion to time-homogeneous diffusions, closing the gap between analytic and probabilistic treatments of elastic killing used in recent applied models.

papers.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
papers.abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

papers.title: Zariski-constructible functions of class $\mathcal{C}^k$
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a real closed field. A Zariski-constructible subset of $R^n$, $\mathcal{ZC}$-set for short, is a Boolean combination of algebraic subsets of $R^n$. Euclidean closed Zariski-constructible subsets of $R^n$ are the closed subsets of a Noetherian topology finer than the Zariski topology of $R^n$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$. Let $U\subset R^n$ be a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set. We say that a function $f:U\to R$ of class $\mathcal{C}^k$ is a Zariski-constructible function, $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function for short, if its graph is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-set. For instance, regular and $k$-regulous functions on $R^n$ are $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions. We show that the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open set is way richer, even for $k=\infty$, although $\infty$-regulous functions are just regular. Then, we extend the notion of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function over any $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. This paper is mainly devoted to the study of the geometric and algebraic properties of the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(X)$ of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$. From now on, assume that $k\in\mathbb N$. We show that $\mathcal{ZC}$-closed subsets $X$ of $R^n$ are exactly the zero loci of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $R^n$. We show that the Nullstellensatz holds in the ring $\mathcal{ZC}^k(U)$, where $U$ is a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open subset of $R^n$, and that this ring is radically principal. As a consequence of the Nullstellensatz, we prove that any $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-function on a $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed subset $X$ of $R^n$ extends to a $\mathcal{ZC}$-open neighborhood $U$ of $X$. Then, we translate our results into the language of sheaves of $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-functions on $\mathcal{ZC}$-locally closed sets, from which we deduce a $\mathcal{ZC}^k$-version of Cartan's theorems A and B.

papers.title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
papers.abstract: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.

papers.title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. Under bounded actions, a regular benchmark policy and exact empirical minimization, the expected objective gap to the benchmark policy is at most of order $N^{-1/2}+\sqrt{N(1+\log N)/n}$, with $N$ the feature width per output coordinate and $n$ the number of paths. At fixed sample size the two terms trade off in $N$, and balancing them gives $N\asymp\sqrt{n/\log n}$.
